publications.title: Electric Vehicle Challenges Continue
publications.description:
A day in the automaker life...
For several years, global OEMs have made dramatic shifts to EV-dominated lineups. But nowhere does demand exceed cost-to-build, so it has been a tough selling climate for dealers. The only market exception is China, where incentives and government mandates drive brisk sales.

Elsewhere, consumer preferences are ever-changing, forcing automakers to adapt to software-defined vehicles, hybrids, and even revert to traditional internal combustion options to counter the uncertain market acceptance of EVs. The payback on an EV is still too long, nearly seven years, and must move to four years to make economic sense for the average car buyer.

Add to this even more "don't see" issues, and here are just a few...
- High cost of repairs and insurance.
- Scarcity of certified technicians - which means you wait up to 4X longer for service intervals.
- Disposal policies do not exist - so batteries end up in landfills - not a very green alternative.
- Warranty of EVs doesn't match traditional vehicles - which makes consumers angry.
- Part replacement queues don't exist because suppliers are struggling.
- Cold weather, range limit, on-demand charging, fires, battery failure - all are volatile business issues.

Not implying that electric is a bad option, it is a great choice - but first we must "test, validate and resolve" some of the above problems. Especially so to benefit average consumers. Sometimes new products are designed and go quickly through engineering stages to commercial adoption. Sometimes they shouldn't.

The good news? Opportunities are everywhere right now in the auto space, and we can re-tool and align our thinking to match the markets we serve, as we create a common-sense bridge to the future - which should include EVs.
#EV #global #problemsolving #createdemand #qualityfirst #infrastructure

publications.title: Impact of Reshoring US Manufacturing Jobs
publications.description:
Today Hyundai is expected to announce a $21 billion investment in U.S. manufacturing, including a $5 billion Louisiana steel plant that will employ 1,500 people, according to CNBC. 

Along with Apple, Oracle, Nvidia, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, Japan’s SoftBank, and others making big US investments, these reshoring efforts will provide overdue manufacturing localization.

Why does this trend matter? These investments, as the new plants are built, will restore Rust Belt towns that were devastated in the 1970's. As a kid who grew up in a factory town in the Midwest, I saw first-hand how my hometown and others became almost extinct. They've hung on by a thread. Some never made it.

The manufacturing contribution to GDP is not only the new factory jobs themselves, but the immense positive impact of innovation, supporting exports, the ripple effect across other sectors, including new service jobs and infrastructure. That impact is what's missing in the US today.

The National Association of Manufacturers estimates that for every $1 spent, a manufacturing job yields an economic impact of nearly $3. 
Ann Arbor, MI-based Center for Automotive Research (CAR) goes further and tells us that every UAW-GM job supports 10 other jobs in the U.S. economy.

The coming new auto sector jobs (and others) will transform our American landscape. So the end game here is all about new jobs, restoring towns and cities, and the rebirth of the middle class I remember growing up. 

Will there be some hurdles? Yes, of course. Workforce retraining, alignment with GenAI and new cleantech, integrating with bots and drones, will cause short-term pain while factory towns and communities are being built.

We've lived through decades of storm clouds, abandoned factories, and vanishing towns littering our US skylines. Here's hoping that what's ahead will bring hope, happiness and bigger paychecks to our middle class working families.

publications.title: Eyes of the Industry on Detroit - The Motor City's Moment to Shine
publications.description:
Motown takes the industry stage and basks in the glow. While the Geneva and Frankfurt auto shows have ceased to exist, the Detroit Auto Show has returned to its traditional January timeslot with bold plans that build on past traditions while launching new interactive and immersive experiences.

The Detroit Auto Show is returning to its roots: devoting more time to simply let consumers check out the cars, SUVs, and trucks, compare prices and features. This is a significant change from years ago when automakers spent millions of dollars at the auto show planning flashy news conferences to introduce concept vehicles and new technologies ― many of which never commercialized for months or years, if ever.

Winners of the 2025 North American Car, Truck and Utility Vehicle of the Year are the Honda Civic Hybrid, Ford Ranger and Volkswagen ID Buzz. These vehicles reflect breakthrough quality, design and performance achievement. But, meanwhile, vehicle pricing has soared since the pandemic.

So, what’s next? Expect more change and transformation for the rest of this decade and beyond. Will we see more EV platforms? Or will fuel cell technology research gather more momentum? My vote is we will see a much wider array of hybrids – they are significantly more reliable in this industry-wide testing and validation phase, plus they are more affordable for average consumers.

Industry needs to solve the “last mile” infrastructure and mobility issues so that consumers have true connected transportation choices. Key benefits will be increased traffic safety, reduction of fatalities, greater transportation options for seniors and personal mobility integration, especially in urban areas.
But the issues driving technology alliances between auto and tech companies run wide and deep, sometimes creating blurred lines between who is competitor and who is partner.

Keeping Michigan a destination of choice for new mobility startup companies is a key industry objective in 2025. Detroit rocks!

publications.title: A Strike Against Progress In Motown
publications.description:
Pay raises, yes, but the true win for the UAW is about the long-term future of its workers.
Making cars is already evolving with the arrival of new technologies, smart factories and AI - which may soon cut out many line workers.
As EVs proliferate the industry, the number of critical vehicle parts required moves from thousands to less than a few hundred.
That alone would suggest that the UAW should focus on certifying the up-skilling of its workforce to match the coming production requirements as the industry dramatically shifts.

The UAW must address the real and present workplace issues, like co-sponsoring technical programs that build new trade skills, training in robotics, AI and systems programming, and promoting other ways to create value on the shop floor, and shift their thinking to more risk-based compensation plans. If, as they claim, record profits are here or right on the verge, then championing profit-sharing plans versus traditional, unaffordable pensions, is a genuine path forward.

The auto business takes on a moving target virtually every day and success is mostly found in the rear-view mirror in such a fast-changing industry. The UAW must set aside the fear and loathing tactics of last century and instead help members acquire new skills so that they truly can out-compete the rest of the world this century.

In the fierce global wars to build and hold markets, issues of principle, fighting and losing may seem to be a better outcome than compromise. But is inflicting pain preferable to gaining new perspectives of leading-edge technologies? 

In the end, if there is revenue to make and if indeed the pie is increasing, why not collaborate? A lesson that the union and automakers must embrace or risk their hard-earned momentum and labor/technology advantages gained since the Great Recession. Pay attention to the merits of new models of moderate thinking and help the other side see the middle ground.

It starts by finding your way to the bargaining table.

publications.title: Driving Toward Autonomous Vehicles
publications.description:
DETROIT, Michigan – 2014 saw U.S. light vehicle sales increase for the fifth year in a row. The excellent performance of the U.S. automotive market since the Great Recession of 2009 has helped drive the country’s overall economic recovery. As we near the end of the second quarter of 2015, volumes continue to grow at a rapid pace in the U.S. market.
Meanwhile, leading-edge development continues to pour into the auto space, as new organic innovation and technology initiatives emerge nearly each week. Grabbing headlines and most of the recognition is the autonomous car, or Self-Driving Vehicle (SDV), which is the industry’s most ambitious commercial campaign. Although the Google car typically receives the majority of the public’s attention, there are other contributors, subplots and issues for the SDV. Here are a few highlights:
The timeline to realization of a self-driving car is accelerating but still a long way off.  As personal mobility and smart connectivity drive new products shaping the automotive industry, driver assistance systems are guiding the U.S. market toward the fully autonomous car. Rapid industry adoption of disruptive technologies is making such intelligent transport systems possible. 
But today’s autonomous car is clearly in a knowledge-gathering period and, from an engineering standpoint, we’re squarely in the applied design development phase, which means more time must be spent testing and validating the steps necessary to meet engineering, legal, safety and regulatory standards – most of which aren’t even on the drawing board yet.
The best guess is that we will see key phases of autonomous driving introduced over the next five years, and a more fully autonomous SDV seems likely to be available early next decade.

publications.title: The Rise of the South
publications.description:
Will the U.S. auto industry’s massive R&D infrastructure based in Michigan ever depart for southern climates? Not anytime soon, and probably never. With fully 75% of the entire U.S. auto industry’s research and development assets located in four Michigan counties (Oakland, Wayne, Macomb and Washtenaw), that isn’t likely to change in the foreseeable future. 
However, there have been serious efforts by the German (Volkswagen, BMW, Mercedes-Benz) and Asian (Nissan, Toyota, Honda, Hyundai) OEMs to aggregate more R&D focus in the southern states where they have located significant manufacturing investment. 
More public-private partnerships are popping up in the south, and academic alliances such as Clemson University’s International Center for Automotive Research (CU-ICAR) brokering research deals between OEMs, traditional suppliers, and organic technology companies new to the auto space.
The rise of the south is a strategic shift that is rooted in the technological, economic, and human capital changes the industry is facing. It is not a “North versus South” showdown, or even a domestic versus non-domestic OEM issue. The deeper challenge is how the industry will navigate new forces converging in the industry – alternative powertrain solutions, urbanization in emerging world markets, emissions worries, vehicle connectivity, autonomous driving, and more – and be prepared to take all the help it can get, regardless of geography. Building a technology hub in the south to complement the R&D ecosystem in Palo Alto, Michigan and Boston is the long view.

publications.title: Deeper Problems in Mexico
publications.description:
Today Mexico is seeing renewed investment as cross-region shipments have become mostly obsolete. The dollars began to return to Mexico by the end of last decade. Mexico is experiencing a re-emergence in the auto space because rising regional energy prices coupled with new logistical planning tools have made the cost of shipping component parts exclusively from China a thing of the past. Fortifying Mexico’s prominance as a major manufacturing player again is its desirable proximity to North American and South American markets, and co-location requirements that have brought OEMs and suppliers together in-country.

Over the past ten years automakers including Nissan, General Motors, Honda, Volkswagen, Chrysler, Ford and Audi have made significant investments to expand production and build new plants in Mexico.  We are now seeing Mexico become an export base to Europe and Latin America, as well as to the U.S. and Canada as its total landed cost becomes a competitive advantage when compared with other global manufacturing locations. 

But warning flags have been raised as serious quality issues are spiking south of the border.  As OEMs ramped up production in Mexico to take advantage of low labor costs, timely free-trade agreements, and insulation from fluctuations in the yen, they overlooked the dire impact of a market not ready for prime time. With the rise of new investment has come nagging challenges with vehicle completion and delivery. One example is Honda’s new $800 million plant in Celaya, about 160 miles northwest of Mexico City, which has been struggling to meet demand amid problems caused by an unskilled labor force, language barriers, and logistics issues that were unforeseen.

publications.title: Natural Gas Has Arrived
publications.description:
With gasoline prices soaring over the past several years, many American car buyers are looking at available powertrain alternatives for relief, and chief among those options is compressed natural gas (CNG). The private commercial drilling phenomenon in this country has propelled the U.S. to overtake Russia as the world’s largest natural gas producer. Fracking, the primary natural gas extraction method, while controversial with environmentalists and others, has built our supplies enough to meet current U.S. consumption for 100 years. What happens next could have a revolutionary impact on American business and influence our economy and job growth positively if we seize the opportunity in front of us today. 
As noted recently in Bloomberg News, “To truly upend the global energy balance, the U.S. must also revolutionize demand. And the only way to do that is to get natural gas into what has always been the greatest prize: light trucks, 18-wheelers, government and delivery fleets, and, of course, private (passenger) cars…”
What can we expect next? As CNG makes its broader entry into the auto space, we should expect to see good economic news. Most of the natural gas consumed in the United States is domestically produced, and the resulting effect will be the reduction of our overall dependence on foreign oil. We have the natural gas resources to grow supply and lower overall cost of oil production and delivery, but what’s really needed is a consistent sustainable energy policy from Washington and the willingness to let private markets operate more unfettered. This alone solves not only many automotive industry problems but would create dynamic paths of growth for our entire U.S. economy.

publications.title: Doing Things the Right Way
publications.description:
It was just a little over two months ago that General Motors was riding the crest of the ultimate wave: a double win at the Detroit Auto Show with the Chevy Corvette taking Car of the Year and the Silverado earning Truck of Year honors, and longtime GM executive Mary Barra rightfully wowing the industry as its first-ever female CEO. Sprinkle in impressive 2013 sales growth and record profits and, other than the lousy weather, you couldn’t script a better start to 2014 for GM. That is, until the news of the recall…
Enter the revelation of defective ignition switches installed in the Chevy Cobalt, Saturn Ion, and Pontiac Solstice models last decade that have resulted in at least 13 deaths, 31 crashes and this month a recall of 1.6 million GM vehicles. Just sixty days after basking in the glow of her ground-breaking achievement, today Mary Barra must shift to crisis management that has real survival implications for General Motors.
As Detroit Free Press columnist Tom Walsh stated, the recall “may not prove to be a crushing blow for GM, if managed smartly with urgency and transparency.” He’s right, and the baptism by fire facing Barra could prove to be a positive, defining moment for her and the company. Her steady and thoughtful approach in this situation could pay dividends and set a standard for other CEOs to do things the right way when complex problems arrive at their door.

publications.title: Engineering Call of Duty
publications.description:
Overcoming engineering challenges is more than a technical goal…it is a major business hurdle.  As the challenges and shortages are met and new productivity standards are realized, entire global organizations hang in the balance. Matching the speed of innovation and fast-paced change demands leverage of all resources throughout the entire company. Change or die.
Engineering shortages don’t simply slow down product development, they are preventing on-time vehicle launches, crimping innovation-to-market plans, and causing a negative cost and profit drain everywhere. Monetization of technology is crucial and the best path to get there is through more effective and efficient product and engineering processes. Achieving engineering productivity is more than just clearing a technical hurdle because doing so creates competitive advantage that can be felt enterprise-wide.
Operational transformation must be guided by proven productivity improvement methodology. These new methods should be targeted at identifying the needed productivity gains and then implementing structured changes to deliver those gains. In that context, the engineering call of duty is clear: to close the gap between knowledge and commercially viable applications that deliver real aspirational value to car buyers worldwide. Not for the fainthearted as we forge forward into 2014, but for me it is inspiring how the auto business shows us that being world class is a moving target every day and success is usually found only in the rear-view mirror.

Hazem Galal is a Senior Partner at PwC Middle East and PwC’s Global Smart Mobility Co-leader. He has expertise in strategy formulation and implementation for cities and local government entities in multiple domains, including smart cities. He was the project adviser for the World Economic Forum’s research on many cities projects and publications. Hazem was a member of the WEF’s Global Future Council on Cities and Urbanization for six years and is currently a member of the WEF's Global Innovation and Impact Council. Hazem was also the co-chair for the working group on city connectivity , as part of the ITU and UNESE’s initiative Smart Sustainable Cities. Hazem is the co-author of the book “Delivering Sustainable Competitiveness - Revisiting the organising capacity of cities”. He worked with cities and state governments around the world in both developed and developing cities conditions.
Hazem is a frequent speaker at many global conferences focusing on smart and sustainable cities, hosting mega events, innovation organized by national governments, the World Economic Forum, World Bank, the G20, the BRICS, the Asian Development Bank, the Inter-American Development Bank and the United Nations.  He has been hosted as an expert on several occasions by leading media channels such as the BBC, CNBC, CNN, Russia Today and Channel News Asia. publications.description:
Inclusive and sustainable growth is vital for social harmony and equity among city inhabitants. The New Urban Agenda, recently adopted at Habitat III in Quito, sets out the key priorities and goals for holistic urban development. However, lack of sufficient public funds, limited capabilities and unclear governance structures often hinder the realization of a city’s vision for sustainable urban development. Collaboration of all stakeholders is fundamental as government entities alone cannot address the growing urbanisation challenges.

Both the government and private sector must play their part to deliver on the objectives of the New Urban Agenda by prioritising their actions to reflect a city’s unique context, immediate and long term priorities and the created impact to achieve sustainable development

publications.description: This book provides insight into the complex issue of delivering sustainable competitiveness by analysing a number of innovative urban development strategies in context. Questions and topics addressed include: how can new legacies of city events be secured; how can clean technology industries be nurtured through urban regeneration initiatives; and how can the impact of urban safety strategies be enhanced? These and other pivotal questions are explored through close attention to the enabling factors linking ideas with results, such as distributed leadership, collaboration, communication and experimentation. Combining case studies from Europe, Africa, South America and Southeast Asia, the book provides a truly international perspective on the potentials and limitations of a new generation of urban development and competitiveness strategies.

about:
Risk Management Senior Executive Officer with over 20 years of leadership experience in financial services, specializing in technology risk management, data governance, AI/ML risk mitigation, and regulatory strategy. 

Winner of the University of Chicago Booth MBA Global New Venture Challenge for developing the architecture of an Artificial Intelligence governance and compliance SaaS application, merging innovative technology with regulatory solutions. 

Recipient of the FFIEC Outstanding Achievement Award for pivotal contributions to enhancing technology and data supervision capabilities within Federal Financial Regulatory Agencies. 

Commissioned Federal Examiner with a proven expertise in leading end-to-end audit functions, risk transformation initiatives, and IT risk assessments aligned with COSO, NIST, and FFIEC standards. Certified CPA, CIA, CDPSE, CISA, and CRISC, with a track record of driving innovation and delivering measurable value.

CORE COMPETENCIES

Risk Management and Compliance: Expertise in enterprise risk management, COSO, NIST, and FFIEC compliance, focusing on integrated risk management tools and frameworks.

Audit Innovation: Proficient in implementing advanced auditing tools, including predictive analytics, AI-driven dashboards, and continuous improvement methodologies.

Regulatory Strategy: Deep knowledge of OCC, CFPB, PCI, SOC2 compliance standards, GDPR, and EU AI Act, with proven success in aligning audit practices to regulatory expectations.

Technology Risk Management: Payments Data Strategy, Banking Transaction Oversight, Regulatory Data Policy Adherence, Enterprise Data Strategy Road mapping, Stakeholder Alignment. Skilled in IT risk assessments, data privacy, and cybersecurity compliance.

Leadership and Collaboration: Track record of managing diverse, high-performing teams and fostering inclusivity, enhancing team alignment and innovation.

Technical Proficiency: Python, Vibe Coding, OpenAI API, Model Context Protocol (MCP), Product Requirements Document (PRD), Replit, Cursor, V0, Claude, AWS Bedrock, Amazon Q, Vertex AI, AWS SageMaker, SageMaker Clarify, RLHF, RAG, LLMops, MLOps, RSA Archer, Tableau, Power BI, Databricks Data Lakehouse, Databricks Unity Catalog, AI/ML risk governance, and Blockchain Strategy.

As AI becomes integral to how businesses operate, compete, and grow, I partner with organizations to define success, reimagine business models, and deploy AI-driven solutions at scale. My focus is on enabling clients to innovate faster, bring new offerings to market with speed and precision, and operate responsibly—building trust and value for the future.

publications.title: Enabling AI with Confidence - A Practical Playbook for Risk and Compliance Leaders
publications.description:
In this thought-provoking paper, Enabling AI with Confidence: A Practical Playbook for Risk & Compliance Leaders, my co-authors and I push back on a common belief that AI in U.S. financial services is operating in a regulatory vacuum and that firms must wait for new “AI laws” before putting meaningful governance in place. 

We show how existing expectations around accountability, transparency, and operational effectiveness already apply to AI, so leaders can manage it as part of enterprise risk rather than a standalone tech issue. 

The paper distills these expectations into an actionable approach for clearer guardrails, stronger oversight, and safer AI adoption at scale.

publications.title: Reimagining the bank examination process: A collaborative, bank-led approach
publications.description: In this thought-provoking edition of PwC's Our Take - [Reimagining the bank examination process: A collaborative, bank-led approach] - we propose a model under which banks that meet financial and compliance standards can shift from retrospective, supervisor-led exams to a forward-looking process driven by bank-created issues management action plans. This new approach is enabled by advances in technology—GenAI, ML, NLP, and predictive monitoring—that deliver near-real-time risk and control analysis, clearer root-cause insights, and more proactive risk management

publications.title: Using Hidden Markov Models to Capture Temporal Aspects of Ultrasound Data in Prostate Cancer
publications.publishedAt: IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM) · Jan 1, 2015
publications.description: Recent studies highlight temporal ultrasound data as highly promising in differentiating between malignant and benign tissues in prostate cancer patients. Since Hidden Markov Models can be used for capturing order and patterns in time varying signals, we employ them to model temporal aspects of ultrasound data that are typically not incorporated in existing models. By comparing order-preserving and order-altering models, we demonstrate that the order encoded in the series is necessary to model the variability in ultrasound data of prostate tissues. In future studies, we will investigate the influence of order on the differentiation between malignant and benign tissues.

publications.title: Increasing the Discovery Power and Confidence Levels of Disease Association Studies: A Survey
Genetic Feature Selection Using Dimensionality Reduction Approaches: A Comparative Study
publications.description: The recent decade has witnessed great advances in microarray and genotyping technologies which allow genome-wide single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) data to be captured on a single chip. As a consequence, genome-wide association studies require the development of algorithms capable of manipulating ultra-large-scale SNP datasets. Towards this goal, this thesis proposes two SNP selection methods; the first using Independent Component Analysis (ICA) and the second based on a modified version of Fast Orthogonal Search. The first proposed technique, based on ICA, is a filtering technique; it reduces the number of SNPs in a dataset, without the need for any class labels. The second proposed technique, orthogonal search based SNP selection, is a multivariate regression approach; it selects the most informative features in SNP data to accurately model the entire dataset. The proposed methods are evaluated by applying them to publicly available gene SNP datasets, and comparing the accuracies of each method in reconstructing the datasets. In addition, the selection results are compared with those of another SNP selection method based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA), which was also applied to the same datasets. The results demonstrate the ability of orthogonal search to capture a higher amount of information than ICA SNP selection approach, all while using a smaller number of SNPs. Furthermore, SNP reconstruction accuracies using the proposed ICA methodology demonstrated the ability to summarize a greater or equivalent amount of information in comparison with the amount of information captured by the PCA-based technique reported in the literature. The execution time of the second developed methodology, mFOS, has paved the way for its application to large-scale genome wide datasets.

publications.title: Single nucleotide polymorphism selection using independent component analysis
publications.publishedAt: Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC), 2010 Annual International Conference of the IEEE · Aug 31, 2010
publications.description: Bioinformatics research in genome wide association studies necessitates the development of algorithms capable of manipulating very-large datasets of Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNP). To facilitate such association studies, we propose a novel framework for SNP selection using Independent Component Analysis (ICA). Compared to previous ICA-based methods, our framework works as a filtering technique to reduce the number of SNPs in a dataset, without the need for any class labels. We evaluate the proposed method by applying it on three published SNP datasets, and comparing the results to SNP selection methods based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA). Our results show the capability of ICA to capture an increased or matching amount of information from the datasets.

publications.title: Fast orthogonal search for genetic feature selection
publications.publishedAt: Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC), 2010 Annual International Conference of the IEEE · Aug 31, 2010
publications.description: In this paper, we present the application of a multivariate regression approach, fast orthogonal search, to select the most informative features in Single Nucleotide Polymorphism data, and to use these features to accurately model the entire data. Our results on two published datasets show very high accuracies in capturing the hidden information in the sequence of studied SNPs. The execution time for our developed methodology is very short and paves the way for its application to large-scale genome wide datasets.

about: Real estate leader with broad expertise supervising class-A commercial office and retail portfolios in excess of 20 million sq ft & $1.4 billion in value, primarily for Fortune 500 financial services and telecommunications companies. Over 15 years of experience in corporate real estate, including a successful history of domestic and international program oversight, with a focus on portfolio optimization, financial analysis, and project management

experience.description:
Strategic leader of a 7M sq ft portfolio of class-A commercial office leases, with an annual budget of $450 million, supporting all 57,000+ employees in the United States, Mexico, and Global Acceleration Centers in India & SE Asia:

•	Strategic Leadership: Formulates the long-term strategic real estate plan for over 100 office locations, leading a team of 40+ professionals (Strategy / Space Management / Design / Construction / Finance / Business Intelligence).

•	Business Case Development: Prepares executive business cases, utilizing occupancy analytics and financial analysis to identify optimal solutions. Presents recommended action to internal clients and senior leadership for project approval.

•	Client Relationship Management: Acts as trusted advisor to market & local office leadership, along with national line-of-service CxO executives, to ensure real estate strategy aligns with business strategy.

Strategic manager of an 8MM SF portfolio of owned/leased commercial office space, with an annual budget of $50MM, achieving 50% SF reductions & annualized savings of over $10MM:

•	Portfolio Optimization: Develops the long-term strategic plan for a multi-state portfolio of administrative, call-center, and distribution properties, cost-effectively optimizing workplace occupancy to a metric of 175 SF/employee.

•	Business Unit Planning: Partners with business unit leadership, managing a cross-functional team of client relationship managers, space planners & transactions managers, to ensure strategic plans are aligned with business outlook.

•	Business Case Development: Prepares tactical business cases, utilizing occupancy analytics and financial analysis (NPV/Payback/IRR) to identify optimal solutions. Presents business cases to clients and to real estate senior leadership for project & funding approvals.

•	Project Execution: Executes approved projects, coordinating a team of construction managers, IT implementers, facility managers, business leads & external vendors (brokers, contractors), to ensure compliance with lease expiration dates.

Served as Global Finance Manager of a $250MM, multi-national re-brand/renovation program for over 2,800 points-of-sale throughout Latin America (Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, Chile, Peru), for Fortune 500 telecommunications client Nextel. Acted as Cash Flow manager of a $60MM portfolio optimization program in Chicago, for financial services client Bank of America:

•	Accounting Supervision: Managed and submitted monthly cost tracker reports to finance department, providing control over local market Oracle databases and conducting FX variance reconciliation exercises.  Audited monthly accruals reported by local markets, ensuring compliance with technical accounting requirements.

•	International Program Oversight: Designed and implemented processes for international financial reporting of all budget commitments and expenditures. Trained international team of budget analysts, monitoring all reporting deadline and data accuracy requirements.

•	Financial Planning & Analysis: Led weekly strategic budget meetings, analyzing and interpreting financial data regarding risks & opportunities, providing recommendations to client for budget transfers and funding requests

•	Cash Flow Forecasting: Tracked and controlled expenditures across 200 real estate tenant improvement projects across ten states, including oversight of purchase order and invoice processes. Reduced cash flow forecasting variance from 150% to under 1%.

Project manager responsible for the scope, schedule, and budget for a $300MM, 1.6MM SF, two 50-story tower multi-family real estate development in downtown Chicago, reporting to investment management client Blackrock:

•	Owner Representation: Represented ownership on behalf of investors in owner-architect-contractor (OAC) meetings, providing project direction and conflict resolution on a weekly basis. Responsible for preparing and distributing monthly reports to investment and lender partners for review on quarterly calls.

•	Construction Management: Developed tracking system to monitor and expedite construction progress, obtaining the certificate of occupancy two months in advance and 5% under budget. Acted as communications liaison between building operations and general contractor during building start-up phase.

•	Retail Development: Conducted feasibility studies for retail space subdivisions, authoring retail work-letters, contracts, requests for proposals (RFP’s), and auditing lease agreements. Developed retail budgets, conducted bidding & negotiation process with contractors, and monitored construction schedules.

Led interdisciplinary teams of architects & engineers during the construction document & contract administration phases of numerous build-to-suit corporate headquarters, ensuring fast-track schedule obligations were met:

•	Consultant Management: Managed multi-discipline team of consultants throughout construction document and administration phases for a 20 floor, 475K SF corporate headquarters in Fort Worth for Pier 1 Imports.

•	Schedule Management: Coordinated the daily architect / engineer team efforts to review contractor submittals and RFIs in an expedited manner for a 1.2MM SF corporate headquarters campus in Sacramento for CalPERS.

•	Construction Administration: Single point of responsibility for the review of all product data and shop drawing submittals, ensuring compliance with construction documents and specifications before granting approval.

Served as project architect for the schematic design & design development phases of various ground-up, Class-A commercial office buildings, consistently exceeding budget and schedule goals:

•	Design Development: Directed a team of architects throughout the fast-track design development phase for a 40 floor, 1.1MM SF corporate HQ in Houston for AIM Investments, ensuring client delivery in under 10 weeks.

•	Floor Plan Optimization: Collaborated with engineering teams to develop an efficient building core for a 15 floor, 375K SF corporate HQ in Atlanta for Rubbermaid, in order to maximize rentable lease depths for ownership.

•	Cost Savings: Identified and implemented various value-engineering opportunities for a 5 floor, 125K SF corporate HQ in Atlanta for Wachovia, maximizing project value while protecting the integrity of the design.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Softgoods Engineering Manager at Meta
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: May 30, 2023, Matt worked with Chris on the same team
receivedRecommendations.description:
I had the pleasure of working with Chris for several years while we were both at Whipsaw. Our biggest project together was the Leitz Icon label printer, where I was the lead mechanical engineer and Chris was the lead industrial designer. I found Chris to be highly collaborative as we worked together on different ways to arrange the key components (paper cartridge, print head, cutter, etc) that would meet the mechanical needs, while also creating a unique and interesting form factor for the product. As we worked through the detailed design and into production, Chris challenged me to find solutions to problems important to ID, such as maintaining zero draft on the outside of the product while visually and tactilely hiding any resultant parting lines from slides and lifters. I think he struck the perfect balance of understanding and working within the realities of mechanical design and manufacturing (critical to actually shipping products!), while working collaboratively with the ME team to question assumptions and find solutions that met the ID goals. The result was not only a great product, but a positive team culture and happy client. 

I would highly recommend working with Chris if you get the opportunity!

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Research Scientist and entrepreneur in the field of analytical instruments.
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: April 16, 2022, Philippe was Chris’ client
receivedRecommendations.description:
I had the chance to work with Chris several times over the last decade and it's been nothing less than an eye-opening experience for me.
As a trained scientist and engineer, I assumed I had all the tools I needed to develop the products my clients needed (analytical instruments for scientists).  I naively thought the industrial design part would organically flow down from the technical design.  Boy was I wrong.  We managed to launch two products, and if we became proud of what we had given birth to, it certainly was not based on how the babies looked.
A few years later, for a new round of product development with a bit more cash in the bank, I was able to bring in Chris (then at Whipsaw) at the last hour to do what he could to improve the design of our new product.  It was way too late in the development cycle, yet Chris managed to work around all our constraints and made dramatic improvements to our product looks and user experience.
Fast forward a few years, new business, new product, I hired Chris as early as I could in the development of our first product to guide me in its design.  With added design flexibility, new manufacturing options, and more freedom to explore, Chris was able to draw a clear target before I started shooting arrows.  He gave us a clear vision of what the product should look like, and had a very deep impact on what the product eventually became.  We did everything we could with our mechanical design to match his original sketches, and whenever hitting a roadblock, we ran things by him for guidance.
This exchange is invaluable in the design process.  As a lead technical designer, I easily get caught in the thousands of technical details of system performance,  mechanical parts design, PCB layout, or assembly procedures.  Adding industrial design on top of this makes everything foggy.  It takes someone like Chris to step back and look at the product from a different perspective.
Chris’ ability to listen, understand engineering constraints, and come back with a beautiful and elegant design has been astounding.  Chris has also shown much patience in teaching us the basics of design language.  Our shared passion for motorcycles provided a common ground to bounce ideas or test each other’s language.
It’s been an absolute pleasure working with Chris, I am looking forward to the next opportunity to develop a product together.

receivedRecommendations.description:
I worked with Chris for over 5 years at Hewlett Packard in the PhotoSmart Printer Division.  Chris was the lead designer on some of the most innovative and ground breaking photo printers. He was an active contributor to a design language that spread beyond our group and helped unify the PhotoSmart brand across HP divisions from San Diego to Singapore and Barcelona.  Chris was also an advocate of design beyond the products. He personally conceived, negotiated and won management approval for a Design Lab which became the focal point for displaying concept models, color studies and design presentations including "What is Industrial Design" presentations to management, marketing and our lab of hardware engineers.  I vividly remember one presentation where Chris advocated that the back of a printer should be designed as well as the front. Some "hard core" mechanical engineers took exception. The discussion was vigorous, but Chris kept his cool and in the end the most vocal dissenter was convinced and said "I disagreed because of the 'extra work', but Chris is right".  
I highly recommend Chris and should there be an opportunity to work together in the future, it wouldn't take more than a nanosecond to decide.

slides.title: The need for Business Focused Asset Management System and Strategy
slides.subtitle: Samir Elkafi, MSc, CEM, CFM, CCP, LEED GA, ACIArb, CMCA, CMRP, IAM, AssocRICS, ADDC Cert,IFMA trainer on LinkedIn
slides.description: s FM professional, I am observing how owners and developers (clients) are managing their assets and how they have changed their way of managing it during the pandemic (COVID-19). It’s clear that the current pandemic hit the market heavily and with the uncertainty associated with it, clients and developers are looking for an immediate and significant cost reduction to reduce the financial impact. Consequently, they were very generous in term of reducing the service level (such as response and rectification time) and technical requirements (such as reducing the PPM frequency, or even go with the Run To Fail strategy, without proper analysis and consequences study), the result was, of course, gaining an immediate cost reduction, however, on the other hand; Adopted operating model was not aligned with the client/developer's vision and strategic objectives An immediate un-satisfied end-users, apparently, because of the service level have been compromised (not what they have promised their customers) Increased capital expenditures (CAPEX), since the useful life of assets will be shorter, which means higher asset replacement frequency (what clients saved now, they will pay in the near future and increase their financial obligations) Loss of experienced staff one important point to mention, clients (regardless of their functionality and assets criticality) apply the same strategy, because they are looking for the immediate saving. The main issue here is not the need to rationalizing the cost of managing the organization’s, but the way of choosing and implementing the asset management and reduction strategy. Most importantly, clients must develop asset management system and strategy that has built-in resilient and change management capability that allow them to be stable against both internal and external changes. A point to remember, asset management strategy and system that success in one organization does not means it will be successful in other organizations, thus, each organization must develop an asset management strategy and system that suit their capability, flexible, aligned with their vision and assist them to achieve their strategic objectives and all these must be done within the available budget.

publications.title: Create MS Office and Other Application Documents from a Browser — Using a LotusScript Agent, Some HTML, and a Content-Type Flag
publications.description: Learn how to send information from a Domino application to a Web browser and have it open in a non-Domino application like MS Word or Excel, without using COM. This article demonstrates an easy-to-implement technique that overcomes many of the issues that typically bedevil developers who need to disseminate Domino information in specific formats. It’s flexible (you can open documents in real time or have them downloaded to the user’s client), it’s not restricted to a Microsoft Web server, and it’s not server-intensive. Through a series of step-by-step examples, you’ll learn how to: export a Domino view to an Excel spreadsheet, add a dynamic chart, prepopulate Word templates, and create contacts using vCards. You’ll also learn how to force the browser to download a file instead of opening it. Two sample databases, one for release 5 and one for release 6, are available for download from THE VIEW Web site.

publications.title: Simple Methods for Creating HTML-Formatted E-mail in Domino Web Applications and Scheduled Agents
publications.description: This article demonstrates two simple, easy-to-implement, cross-platform methods for sending HTML mail — no large files, no Java code, and no third-party software is required. The first method sends e-mail from a Web-based workflow application after the user submits a document. The second method allows HTML mail to be sent from a scheduled agent. about:
Imran Ilyas is a Partner at PwC and a member of the Advisory Leadership Team, where he leads the firm’s Business & Supply Chain Operations (BSCO) Platform. In this role, he helps clients modernize and manage the core operations that drive their businesses forward. BSCO combines operational consulting, platform delivery, and managed services to enable organizations to increase efficiency, reduce costs, and scale across sectors including Financial Services, Health Industries, Energy & Utilities, Consumer Markets, and Industrials product & services. It integrates leading technologies—including Guidewire, FIS, Fiserv, Epic, Icertis, Maximo, Esri, O9, Blue Yonder, and other modern tools—to enable next-generation contract lifecycle management, sourcing, and procurement capabilities.

With over 30 years of global experience, Imran has led large-scale transformation initiatives across the United States, EMEA and APAC, primarily in the insurance industry. He is widely recognized for his calm leadership style, ability to solve complex problems, and building talent for delivering results at scale. 

In addition to his BSCO role, Imran also serves as a Global and US Guidewire Alliance Leader. PwC’s Global Strategic Guidewire practice includes over 3,000 trained professionals and has successfully delivered 350+ transformation initiatives. ➡️  please visit: pwc.com/us/guidewire 

Throughout his PwC career, Imran has held several pivotal leadership roles: 

• As Functional & Industry Tech Practice Leader, he oversaw a global team of 3,000+ professionals across platforms like Guidewire, Maximo, Icertis, ESRI, and MS Dynamics. 

• As Advisory Delivery Excellence and Quality Leader, he led initiatives to standardize delivery, embed innovation, and scale advanced technologies, including Generative AI. 

• As Global Insurance Advisory Leader, Imran led the development and execution of strategic priorities and propositions that drove business expansion across EMEA, APAC, the Nordics, and North America.

• As a P&C Transformation Leader, he helped build and scale PwC’s core transformation and systems integration capabilities. He is also a frequent speaker at industry forums, offering insights on insurance modernization and digital operations. 

Imran holds an Executive MBA from the Kellogg School of Management, a Master of Science in Computer Science from DePaul University, and a Bachelor of Engineering from the University of Illinois Chicago.

Getting change management right is critical to a PAS transformation’s success.Projects that effectively manage the human elements of change are significantly more likely to deliver on objectives and business results. publications.title: Breaking Down the Core Capabilities of a Successful PAS Transformation
publications.description: Leading carriers are moving beyond the status quo and differentiating themselves by using faster, more flexible approaches to policy administration transformations. They continually map program decisions to the business case, and establish the appropriate committees and frameworks in order to better control changes and meet goals; they rapidly deliver working code in an iterative manner that they can immediately demonstrate to business users; they utilize a policy-specific framework to proactively identify and respond to common issues, which results in more consistent project performance.

publications.title: 10 Steps to Attaining PAS Transformation Success
publications.description: Most new policy admin transformation projects are “challenged” and only a small percentage of them realize the full benefits of change. The goal of a policy administration project should not be the implementation of yet another application, but to deliver transformative capabilities to the business.Effective transformations feature the ability to 1) continually map daily program management decisions to the original benefits case, 2) rapidly deliver code in an iterative manner, and 3) utilize a policy-specific framework to proactively identify and address common project challenges.

publications.title: Eyes on the prize: Implementing fast, flexible policy administration systems in the P&C insurance sector
publications.description: We are seeing an unprecedented level of investment by small to mid-sized carriers whose successful policy administration implementations will provide them the ability to leapfrog larger, better funded competitors through improved product flexibility, speed to market, and lower IT costs. Only 30% of policy administration projects meet the traditional definition of success in terms of time, budget, and scope delivered. And of that 30%, we observe that less than one in three realize the full business benefits. Those carriers who do “optimize” and achieve this rare level of success will be able to leapfrog their competition who may be in the approximately 70% of projects that are challenged or fail outright.

publications.title: Align insurance policy administration system transformation objectives with business drivers
publications.description: Large PAS transformation programs are often delivered late or over budget—if at all—as a result of the magnitude, complexity, and above all, poor upfront planning and alignment with key business drivers. To be successful, leading carriers are aligning PAS transformation objectives with the business drivers that most closely support their corporate strategy and operating environment.

publications.title: 10 Key Considerations to Help Prepare your Conversion Strategy
publications.description: Once an insurance carrier has justified the business case for its policy administration system (PAS) replacement, designed a transformation roadmap, selected a vendor partner, mobilized its implementation, and is successfully managing the execution and change, one daunting task remains: The conversion of its book of business onto the new system. While the beauty of conversion may be that it is a one-time effort, the beast is that every single account and/or policy must be touched in order to effectively complete it. Therefore, an organization should carefully consider what it will take to facilitate a successful conversion effort and minimize the impact on itself, its agency force, and its customers.

publications.title: 10 Keys to Mobilizing Your Policy Admin Implementation
publications.description: Once an insurance carrier commits to replacing its existing Policy Administration system, it is critical that they understand the middle ground between strategy and execution to overcome the many obstacles that stand between their strategic vision and the goal of realizing the benefits of that vision. publications.title: 10 Steps to Choosing a Policy Admin Vendor
publications.description: Once the business case for a policy admin system has been approved, it is imperative that a thorough vendor selection process is performed. publications.title: Designing the PAS Transformation Roadmap
publications.description: After successfully making a business case for transformation, the next major hurdle is determining a sequence for releases. publications.title: How to develop a Business Case for PAS Replacement
publications.description: Most insurance carriers are placing policy administration system (PAS) transformation near the top of their to-do lists because a modern, flexible PAS platform soon will be “table stakes” for any successful carrier. However, insurance executives still struggle with clearly explaining and justifying the benefits of what can be a significant investment.

publications.title: Change Management - The Lynchpin to a Successful PAS Transformation
publications.description: With policy administration system (PAS) transformations at or near the top of most insurance carriers' to-do lists, it is critical for companies to recognize the massive organizational effort required to successfully execute, roll-out, and realize the benefits of a PAS replacement. Because PAS is the lifeline of an insurance carrier's business, undergoing a PAS replacement affects nearly everyone in the organization, as well as agents and insureds. As a result, organizational change management is essential to prepare stakeholders for change and ensure the buy-in required to succeed with a transformation of this magnitude.

headline: IPO Senior Partner, Lead Client Partner to Fast Growth and Emerging Companies
about:
Mike has 34 years of experience focusing on high-growth companies at PwC, including 22 years as a partner, providing accounting, financial reporting and consulting services, while based in PwC’s offices in Chicago, New York, Los Angeles, Seoul and London.  

Mike is a Deals partner and has led PwC’s services around IPOs for many years.  He founded PwC’s IPO services practice, and developed a comprehensive suite of services, from accounting and financial reporting, finance effectiveness, tax, internal controls, treasury, corporate governance, and executive compensation and HR, amongst others, that helps companies prepare for the transaction and for life as a public company.    PwC’s IPO services help companies get to market faster, more efficiently and with fewer surprises.

As a result of his extensive experience with IPOs, he frequently takes on the role of an “IPO Advisor” to help his clients both with their initial registration process, and also with the process of preparing to operate as a public company.

Mike's specific technical knowledge focuses on accounting, financial reporting and project management advice associated with the SEC registration process, accounting for carve-outs, purchase accounting, pro forma financial statements, stock compensation, revenue recognition, segmental reporting, and private equity exit strategies.  

Mike also started PwC’s Capital Markets Advisor (CMA) business, to provide clients with independent and objective advice on capital structure, capital markets, and valuation issues critical to achieving corporate objectives and positioning the company for success.

As a senior partner in the firm, Mike frequently takes on the Lead Client Partner role LCP for many of our largest and most important clients.  In this role he is responsible for bringing all of PwC’s resources to serve our key clients and ensure they receive our highest quality services.  

During his career, Mike has worked on hundreds of IPOs and similar transactions, for both large, as well as IPOs of many smaller and mid-cap privately-held companies for private equity and other sponsors. In recent years many of these companies have gone public through a SPAC transaction.  He is a frequent speaker at conferences and has written many articles and publications on the IPO process and how companies should prepare. He has worked across all industries, and more recently with an emphasis on fast growing technology, software, ecommerce, fintech and consumer goods companies.

publications.title: Subscribe to our weekly Capital Markets Newsletter
publications.description:
PwC's Deals Practice Capital Markets Watch weekly is a snapshot of the IPO market including pricings, withdrawals, headlines for the week and a look to next week.

For companies considering an IPO, it is useful to understand how quickly windows of opportunity can open and close, making it important to be well prepared to enter the market when that moment arrives. Having solid economics, strong fundamentals, and a well-prepared story to market can provide a great foundation for a successful IPO.

publications.title: Navigating Your IPO: How PwC Can Help
publications.description: Most private companies are likely unprepared to be public and will need a significant investment of management time and funds to bring their capabilities up to public company standards. This period of preparation which PwC calls “readiness” can be 12-24 months depending on the maturity of the company. The first step to readiness is an assessment of where your company currently stands. You can’t change what you don’t measure. PwC can help you properly assess and identify gaps in your company’s public company preparedness.

publications.title: Which market? A guide to companies considering a listing in New York, London or Hong Kong
publications.description: To help you determine which options are best for your company, this brochure identifies the main regulatory requirements involved in a listing in some of the current leading global stock exchanges: New York, London, Hong Kong and Singapore.

publications.title: Considering an IPO? Insight into the mindset of institutional IPO investors in the US
publications.description: We recently surveyed 150 institutional investors that invested in IPOs in 2015. Sophisticated investors are asserting more control over the information flow during the IPO process and have access to more information than before.

publications.title: Considering an IPO? An insight into the costs post-JOBS Act
publications.description: The “going public” process changed significantly three years ago with the April 2012 enactment of the Jumpstart Our Business Startups (JOBS) Act. The JOBS Act was designed to spur IPO activity by providing an on-ramp for certain companies, specifically called emerging growth companies (EGCs), to access capital markets and raise capital through an IPO by reducing the reporting requirements. EGCs are now featured prominently in the IPO world, representing 84 percent of the IPOs filed in 2014.

publications.title: Fortified for success Building your company’s risk, controls and compliance ecosystem, for the IPO and beyond
publications.description:
The word “compliance” has the ring of obligation. But for public companies, obligation is the name of the game. Whether you’re an emerging company, a spin-out from a larger public entity, or a mature organization that’s returning to public status after having been taken private, a vital aspect
of IPO preparation should involve rigorously examining your risk management controls and compliance infrastructure through the lens of today’s markets, regulators, and investors. What will they require from you as a public company? In the short and long term, what skills, structures,
and processes will you need to build, reinvent, or reinforce in order to meet those expectations and requirements? And how will you realistically create a forward-looking risk, controls and compliance infrastructure while mired in the financial, reporting, and governance requirements of SEC
registration and stock exchange listing?

publications.title: How non-GAAP Measures Can Impact Your IPO
publications.description: A successful IPO depends on a thorough understanding of how non-GAAP measures can impact the way your company is viewed by potential investors.

publications.title: Roadmap for an IPO:a guide to going public
publications.description:
Going public is a monumental decision that forever changes the way an organization does business. Once listed, a company will be under greater public scrutiny and will have to comply with a range of continuing obligations. Thinking through the requirements and developing an appropriate plan can reduce unexpected pre-initial public offering (IPO) work and post-IPO issues.

The fifth edition of the “Roadmap for an IPO” provides companies considering going public with insight on:

The going public process 
Significant accounting, compensation and tax-related considerations 
Ongoing reporting requirements and operational considerations of being a public company

headline: PwC Partner | Healthcare & Board Leader | PD Advocate
about:
Surrounded by healthcare trailblazers throughout my life, I have spent my career serving the healthcare industry. My leadership in healthcare ranges from global professional services firms to entrepreneurial ventures to Fortune 10 technology companies where I have consulted with the nation’s leading healthcare provider organizations. I enjoy addressing complex transformations, and am passionate about connecting diverse teams and ideas in order to bring real value and results to my clients.  

As a partner in PwC's consulting practice, I serve some of the firm’s largest healthcare clients as lead client partner. I have held many firm leadership roles, including Health Industries Advisory (HIA) Management Consulting Leader, HIA Diversity and Inclusion Leader, Market Portfolio Leader, and Global Engagement Partner. I also serve as a trustee on the PwC Charitable Foundation Board.

My Midwest roots led to the University of Kansas, where I earned Bachelor of Arts (BA), Juris Doctorate (JD) and Masters in Healthcare Administration (MHA) degrees. I have also participated in Harvard Business School's Executive Education program and Northwestern University Kellogg School of Management board development. With philanthropy as a core value, I serve on many local and industry boards. In 2016, I was named a Chicago Business Journal Woman of Influence.

Diagnosed with Parkinson's Disease (PD) at 55, my personal passion is finding a cure and advocating for those living with PD.

headline: Director, PwC | TMT Revenue Transformation | AI-Enabled Revenue Transformation & Complex Q2C
topSkills: Revenue Intelligence • Revenue Transformation • ASC 606 • Artificial Intelligence (AI) • Order to Cash Transformation
about:
I am a Senior Director in PwC’s Management Consulting practice focused on helping Technology, Media, and Telecom (TMT) companies (hyperscalers, SaaS, security, and telcom) scale complex, high-growth revenue models with confidence.

My work centers on Revenue Intelligence — the discipline of preserving deal intent, scaling revenue judgment, and connecting contracts, revenue execution, backlog, and forecast across the deal lifecycle. I specialize in environments where traditional Q2C and ERP implementations fall short due to non-standard deals, consumption-based models, rigid system requirements, and heavy manual interpretation.

I advise clients on how to design approaches for responsibly applying AI as an interpretation and normalization layer — enabling Finance and Accounting to translate how deals are structured commercially into ERP- and audit-ready revenue outcomes. This includes AI-assisted contract interpretation, revenue checklist automation, and governance models that scale judgment without scaling headcount.

Across cloud, software, and telecom, I lead multi-year revenue transformation and stabilization programs spanning SAP BRIM / RAR, Salesforce-based Q2C, backlog and forecast risk, and post-M&A revenue integration. I work closely with Sales, Pricing, RevOps, Accounting, FP&A, and Enterprise AI teams to reduce friction, improve predictability, and elevate Finance’s role as a true business partner.

I partner across Salesforce, SAP, CMAAS (Technical Accounting Advisory), AI, and Customer Transformation teams to deliver outcomes beyond tool implementations, and I focus on building repeatable frameworks, operating models, and playbooks that allow Revenue Intelligence to scale across clients and programs.

about:
As an executive with over 20 years of experience in sustainability, corporate responsibility, and social impact, I am passionate about advancing impact and purpose across sectors and industries. 

I currently lead PwC's Sustainability and Social Impact Center of Excellence. This CoE centralizes internal sustainability and corporate responsibility initiatives for the firm across its US, Mexico and overseas acceleration center footprint. I spearhead the firm's internal environmental and social impact strategies connected with its 80,000 employees, with a strong focus on the firm's net zero commitment. My work activates PwC’s purpose to build trust in society, solve important problems and to create a fulfilling employee experience.

Prior to PwC, I held roles leading enterprise sustainability and human rights initiatives at Wells Fargo and  the corporate responsibility function in North America for ArcelorMittal steel and mining. My experience also includes almost a decade in the social impact sector, working in nonprofits ranging from grassroots to national organizations.

I earned my M.A. in Social Science from The University of Chicago and am an Aspen Institute First Movers Fellow. I currently serve on the Board of Trustees for Net Impact and The Living Classrooms Foundation. Originally from Colorado, I now live in Maryland with my husband and two amazing children. In the winter you can find me chasing powder on the ski slopes, and in the summer I'm at the ballpark hunting for the perfect soft pretzel.

topSkills: Business Strategy • Trusted Advisor to CxOs • Artificial Intelligence (AI) • Emerging Technologies • Global Delivery
about:
At PwC Acceleration Centers, my team drives AI/EmTech innovation and transformative growth, enhancing operational maturity and spearheading emerging technology capabilities. With a strong focus on AI, we pioneer next-generation solutions, fostering resilience through technology across diverse PwC regions. Our strategies align with elevating our global competitive edge, empowering businesses to harness AI for significant impact.

Leading the charge in building high-performing, market-facing teams, I've cultivated a startup culture that emphasizes agility and engineering excellence. Our achievements include deploying a versatile technology stack, from low-code platforms to advanced data analytics, AI, and machine learning models. These initiatives not only accelerate delivery but also ensure the highest quality of service for our clients, thanks to our foundational pillars of innovation, engineering automation, and agile maturity.

experience.description:
As the Commercial Technology and Innovation Leader for PwC Acceleration Centers, I spearhead AI innovation at scale, driving transformative growth across our segments and clients globally. My role encompasses shaping AI and emerging tech (EmTech) capabilities, enhancing operational maturity, and setting the stage for bleeding-edge advancements across diverse PwC regions. I am dedicated to redefining how firms leverage AI, pioneering next-generation solutions, and fostering resilience through technology.

With a specialty in building high-performing, market-facing teams across continents, I lead initiatives that align with strategic goals and elevate our global competitive edge. My work empowers businesses to harness AI for meaningful impact, establishing frameworks that scale AI-driven success across industries. My leadership experience bridges strategy and execution, making innovation a core component of our approach to excellence.

This journey reflects my commitment to driving measurable, forward-looking results, positioning PwC as a global leader in AI transformation and tech-driven growth.

As the Group Director and Head of PwC Labs India, I built a high-performing team from the ground up, cultivating a startup culture that empowered us to achieve engineering excellence at scale. From day one, I was focused on assembling and inspiring a dedicated team, developing and executing strategies for sustainable growth, and ensuring seamless global delivery of cutting-edge solutions. Our work spanned a diverse technology landscape, including low-code/no-code platforms, advanced data analytics, AI models, full-stack development, and comprehensive cloud transformations.

Innovation, engineering automation, operational efficiency, and agile maturity formed the foundation of our approach. I was committed to fostering continuous improvement across these pillars, enabling our team to deliver high-impact products with remarkable speed and uncompromising quality. By embedding a culture of excellence and agility, I positioned PwC Labs India as a powerhouse for advanced technology solutions, setting new standards in the industry and consistently exceeding client expectations.

This role required visionary leadership, strategic insight, and hands-on execution, all of which I delivered while driving results-oriented transformation. By building a team from scratch and aligning our capabilities with evolving market demands, I not only achieved transformative outcomes but also set new benchmarks for quality, scalability, and client impact. This experience reflects my deep commitment to driving digital and engineering excellence at scale, making me a strategic asset for organizations seeking leadership in today’s rapidly evolving landscape.

As the Delivery Head for Banking Programs across MEA, APAC, Canada, and Europe, I led end-to-end program delivery, aligning our initiatives with customer goals and empowering global banking clients to navigate complex FinTech landscapes. My work centered on providing digital thought leadership, particularly in Digital Process Automation (DPA) and Open Banking, to drive transformative solutions that enabled clients to stay ahead in a rapidly evolving industry.

In this role, I was responsible for driving P&L growth for Virtusa across Canada, the Middle East, Europe, and Asia Banking & Financial Services programs. My focus was on delivering value through innovative strategies, fostering digital resilience, and ensuring that our solutions not only met but exceeded expectations in advancing our clients' digital transformation journeys.

As the BPM Practice Head, I was responsible for building in-house competency, driving innovation, and fostering both organic and inorganic growth across our practice portfolio. My focus was on creating robust delivery programs, strengthening customer relationships, and ensuring sustainable revenue growth within the Digital Process Automation (DPA) space.

I also had the privilege of serving as the chief architect for Virtusa's first-ever Pega Technology Innovation Lab—a groundbreaking initiative that received wide recognition and coverage in leading industry publications. This lab became a cornerstone for pioneering solutions, reinforcing our commitment to technological excellence and client success.

As Delivery Director, I led the implementation of new, cutting-edge features to enhance an industry-leading claims platform. In collaboration with our client, I supported the ideation and establishment of a BPM and RPA Center of Excellence, driving streamlined adoption and optimized use of BPM and RPA technologies.

During this time, I also took on the additional role of Solution Consultant and Principal Architect for our Insurance, Healthcare, and Life Sciences SBU, focusing on "start right & execute right" initiatives for new clients. As Head of the Innovation Lab for Insurance, I leveraged Pega, AI, ML, and RPA to develop delivery and solution accelerators, advancing Virtusa's capacity to deliver transformative, high-impact solutions.

Enterprise Architect for a multi-year large and complex transformation program for America's largest P&C Insurance firm. Through his innovative design-thinking he implemented a single claims platform by consolidating 110 different claims systems, catering to the claim adjudication needs of 53 different regulatory countries within the space of 2 yrs.

As a Pega Enterprise Architect, I played a pivotal role in the largest transformation program for a leading global insurance firm. Recognized and certified by prominent market analysts, this groundbreaking initiative represents the most complex and expansive transformation ever undertaken across industries on the PRPC platform. This role required architecting, designing, and implementing a fully reusable and scalable solution for deployment across 50+ countries worldwide.

In my global capacity, I managed diverse stakeholder demands, uniting them towards a single strategic objective. Once fully deployed, this consolidated claims platform will drive multimillion-dollar savings for the insurer, redefining operational efficiency at a global scale.

Previously, I successfully designed and implemented the first-ever case management solution for a prominent utility company in lower Manhattan. This innovative tool was transformative for the industry, quickly gaining recognition as a potential game changer and setting a new standard in utility frameworks.

As a Pega Lead Systems Architect at Virtusa, I was responsible for:

Crafting end-to-end solution architecture for BPM Pega applications.

Driving multimillion-dollar BPM engagements from inception to support.

Translating business requirements into comprehensive business, information, and technology reference architectures.

Leading new business pursuits from RFP initiation through deal closure.

Establishing estimation techniques and productivity metrics within the BPM technology space.

Leading Business Process Improvement (BPI) initiatives.

Ensuring delivery assurance, including estimation, architecture, design, and code review, for all BPM Pega engagements in the HID segment.


This experience reflects my expertise in architecting scalable, high-impact solutions and driving global business transformation through technology.

Responsible for designing and architecting potential BPM solutions to modern-day complex business problems. Involved in new business pursuits, Delivery Assurance, Estimations and managing teams of Tech leads for implementing solutions using cutting edge BPM technologies.
I was the Onsite engagement lead for Cognizant at RBC Canada for  a $4m account. I was responsible for ensuring delivery of BPM PRPC based projects and worked as a Pega LSA as part of my core role.
A PRPC Lead Systems architect responsible for architecture, design and delivery of large scale PEGA engagement in a leading bank in Canada.

As a Techno-Functional System Analyst at HP Mphasis, was responsible for bailing out a long-distressed Pega engagement for one of the leading Canadian bank's wealth management division, and later went on to drive the design & architecture phase and leading a high-performance team to build the solution aligned with stakeholder-expectations. Abhishek achieved this by introducing the agile way to gather and elicit requirements and iterative demo driven design thinking to help customers "see" and "feel" what they needed.  Abhishek, in the process, received several accolades for his efficient analysis of the requirements and timely flawless delivery through his  technical expertise in the PRPC platform.

Based out of Europe, was responsible as a technical lead to ensure the delivery of a large scale Pega Program for the leading Telecom major. Also provided Pega consulting to multiple Project Teams across the country and helped and guided the teams to solve critical technical issues.
A senior PRPC developer who also helped train other new inductees and troubleshoot critical issues.
I was one of the very first guys to be inducted and trained in Pega and one of the first 10 people to be ceritified in CSA examination across India.
