publications.title: Sedatives/Hypnotics
publications.description: Abstract- From the beginning of the twentieth century, bromides enjoyed a significant role in the United States as sedatives. With the advent of barbiturates in the 1940s, the use of bromides waned. The therapeutic use of barbiturates would be replaced by other sedative-hypnotics (S/H) of comparable strength, namely, chloral hydrate and meprobamate. With time, benzodiazepines were marketed as therapeutic substitutes for the traditional S/H as more effective, less toxic, and less addictive anxiolytics. The occurrence of barbiturate abuse and toxicity is relatively low; barbiturates have been replaced with therapeutic alternatives, such as benzodiazepines (BZ) Flumazenil, 1,4-imidazobenzodiazepine, is a BZ antagonist. It competitively antagonizes the binding and allosteric effects of BZs. Flumazenil completely reverses sedative, anxiolytic, anticonvulsant, ataxic, anesthetic, comatose, and muscle relaxant effects. Zolpidem is a non-benzodiazepine hypnotic of the imidazopyridine class. Pharmacologically, it interacts with the gamma-aminobutyric acid–BZ receptor complex and shares some pharmacological properties of BZs.

publications.title: Reproductive and Developmental Toxicity
publications.description: Abstract- Drugs or chemicals that induce structural malformations, physical dysfunction, behavioral alterations, or genetic deficiencies in the fetus, or impair fertility, are referred to as teratogens. Fetal development involves the gradual establishment and modification of anatomical structures from its beginning at fertilization to maturity. Postnatal development begins at birth and progresses to maturity. The first trimester is the period corresponding to embryonic and early fetal development. The main events occurring during the first trimester include: cleavage, implantation, placentation, and embryogenesis. The second trimester corresponds to the third to the sixth month of gestation and is characterized by rapid fetal development of organs and systems. An Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals (EDC) is “an exogenous chemical, or mixture of chemicals, that interferes with endogenous hormonal action". Naturally occurring EDCs, such as the phytoestrogens genistein and coumestrol, are occasionally found in human and animal foods. EDCs target and modulate the endocrine system, which comprises a series of secretory glands and their hormonal secretions.

publications.title: Toxicogenomics
publications.description: Abstract-Toxicogenomics is a relatively new field oriented toward the response of an entire genome to toxicants or environmental stressors. Toxicogenomics encompasses three major objectives: to elucidate the connection between environmental stress and disease susceptibility; to establish proper biomarkers of disease and exposure to toxic substances; and to clarify the molecular mechanisms of toxicity. Target identification aims to distinguish new targets, normally proteins, whose modulation might suppress or prevent disease progression. The advent of technologies that endeavor to associate changes in gene and protein expression or genetic variation with human disease metamorphosed many aspects of medicine. A genome consists of deoxyribonucleic acid. Each genome encompasses all of the information required to assemble and support an organism. Epigenetics is the study of heritable modifications resulting in altered gene function leading to variable phenotype while maintaining an intact genotype. These changes influence the expression of a gene or the properties of its product.

publications.title: Metals
publications.description: Abstract-Metals and their alloys are unquestionably responsible for the transition of human civilizations from their existence in the ancient world, through the Bronze and Iron Ages, to their present modern society. Metals are classified into ferrous and nonferrous materials. Many metallic chemicals, micronutrients, and related compounds are essential for the proper functioning of biological systems wherever they are required in trace amounts. These same biologically relevant substances are toxic with acute or chronic exposure to supraphysiological doses. Chelation therapy is generally associated with the treatment of metal poisoning for the particular goal of decreasing the body burden of the chemicals that have been absorbed and distributed to physiological compartments. Dimercaprol is an effective chelating agent for heavy metal poisoning. Ethylenediaminetetraacetic Acid forms four or six bonds with metal ions and chelates both transition-metal and main-group ions. It is also used as an anticoagulant for stored blood in blood banks and in collection tubes.

publications.title: Epigenetic biomarkers in toxicology
publications.description: Abstract-Epigenetics (EG) encompasses heritable changes in gene expression that do not involve alterations in DNA sequence. Major EG mechanisms include DNA methylation, covalent posttranslational modifications of histone proteins, and noncoding RNAs. These mechanisms mediate transcriptional alterations to orchestrate processes necessary to maintain chromatin structure, as well as differential patterns of gene expression. EG modifications play important roles in processes of cellular development, imprinting, cellular differentiation, X-chromosome inactivation, and transposon silencing. This chapter highlights significant biomedical applications recently identified using EG data—specifically the discovery of novel biomarkers for drug classification, disease diagnosis and prognosis, and for the detection of viable therapeutic targets. In addition, the discussion describes critical functions of EG regulators and the consequences of their malfunction.

headline: Shaping the Future of Healthcare Operations | AI-First Transformation | Payer Strategy & BPaaS Innovation
about:
I help healthcare organizations modernize how they operate and scale - rethinking data, governance, and delivery through an AI-first lens. My work delivers operating models that make complexity manageable: connecting people, processes, and technology to deliver real, lasting results.

At PwC, I lead transformation programs that help payer leaders navigate the shift from traditional claims to next-generation payment ecosystems - integrating automation, analytics, and accountability into the heart of their operations - scaling across the back-office and corporate functions required to do so

I bring deep expertise in payer operating model design, from strategic sourcing to BPaaS transformation, helping clients realign capabilities, vendors, and technology around measurable outcomes.

Focus areas: Healthcare Transformation · AI-Enabled Operations · Payment Innovation (Risk-Bearing & Value-Based Models) · Operating Model & Sourcing (BPaaS) Strategy · Performance & Governance Design · Program Leadership

experience.description:
As a Senior Consultant, I manage various projects encompassing quantitative and qualitative research and analysis, budget management, deliverables, and client relations; lead three team members. Administer ad-hoc analysis for the CEO and Senior Leadership on several key areas, including targeted outreach; provide identification of the staff gaps for current and future projects, and skills awareness. Manage the proposal efforts and identify new opportunities with the existing clients.

My achievements include increasing the staffing resources 10% within 4 months by designing a centralized resource management and staffing process (moved the process from intra-segment staffing to a one shared, end-to-end process); enhanced senior leadership insight on staffing, financial risk, growth opportunities, subcontractor management, and contracts by developing a three-tiered systematic review process on over 60 projects; and administered training sessions with the team members on interviewing strategies and documentation.

In this role, I supplied optimal client delivery services and staff engagement and development; led the internal task team with four junior team members. Conducted stakeholder interviews in documenting internal client processes; established processes in eliminating organizational overlap and surplus.

I also oversaw two special projects:  The Rhode Island Integrated Eligibility Assessment from the Governor’s office of Rhode Island – served as the Operational Lead in resolving backlogs across many programs; and the Kansas Integrated Eligibility Assessment from the Lt. Governor’s office – assessed the newly released KanCare system (supplied vital talent management information).

My successes included resolving the carrier-exchange issues of error tracking and transaction monitoring by developing operational EDI streamlined processes and reports; conducted training sessions with the state employees on new business operating procedures; and received a promotion to Senior Consultant.

I delivered advise to the State Leadership on business process impacts with impending technical releases; updated process documentation for the end-users and provided consulting services on operational decisions in mitigating deployment defects and other issues. Led the technical teams with User Acceptance Testing (UAT) efforts; aligned with future process documentation. Prepared the State Senior Leadership for press releases and news interviews.

During my time in this position, I decreased the change backlog from 6,000 to less than 2,500 within 3 months by leading an Operations Team of 12 Junior Consultants in conducting interviews, research, and data analysis (developed documented process improvements to prevent backlogs and produced 20% processing time savings); reduced the error count from over 1,000 to less than 150 within 4 months and improved resolution times 33% through root-cause analyses with third-party vendors in isolating and solving technical issues (saved customers 3 weeks on average without insurance); lowered IT release impact 25% by consulting with the internal IT teams on and implementing new processes (prepared the State Business Leadership for incoming IT changes); and received a promotion to Consultant.

projects.title: TRACE for Cardiac Arrest Prediction
projects.associatedWith: Associated with University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
projects.description:
The original paper introduces a new unsupervised representation learning method called TRACE which builds on the TNC (Temporal Neighborhood Coding) framework to produce better predictions on ICU data.

The claim we picked from the paper to test is that TRACE will have higher accuracy than baseline models including TNC, CPC, T-Loss, and Supervised with end-to-end encoding on label prediction.

In our attempts to reproduce the paper we were able to prove the claim that TRACE would have a higher accuracy than baseline models in predicting labels, and we were able to do so on a different dataset than what was used in the original paper. This is compelling evidence that the model introduced by the original paper can be used in general for ICU data.

projects.title: Data Science Capstone - Park Visitation Covid Dashboard
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Penn State University
projects.description: Parks are dedicated public spaces that provide valuable benefits to public health and well-being. Park managers and tourism researchers have much to gain by understanding the patterns behind visitations to parks. Better decisions about which parks to allocate resources to can be made, so being able to track park visitation has major policy implications. Visitation data is available from companies like Safegraph; the challenge then is to make the raw visitation data accessible, visual, and otherwise useful for non-technical users.

projects.title: Predicting Oscar Winners using Twitter Sentiment and Movie Ratings
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Penn State University
projects.description:
The Academy Awards, or the Oscars, is the most influential award show in the movie industry where best films of the year are awarded since 1929 (Zauzmer, 2020). Every year, cinephiles and general movie fans all over the world tune in to witness the awards being given out. Predicting the Oscars has also become very popular among movie fans. On the largest prediction site, Gold Derby, there are more than 10,000 users trying to predict the final winners every year. This year, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the film industry is facing unprecedented challenges.

Firstly, there are less blockbuster movies coming out this year due to boxoffice concerns. Looking at this year’s Best Picture nominees, the only “normal” Oscar movies are Mank and The Trial of the Chicago 7. The other six nominees are low-budget independent movies, which are mostly likely not gonna be nominated in a normal year.

Second, the awards season had been prolonged, with the Oscars awards ceremony being postponed to be held on April 25th.

Most importantly, because of the pandemic, all awards season screening had been held online instead of in-person. Many Oscar voters have complained openly because they cannot enjoy the screening in theaters and they cannot converse with other members and get to know their opinions. All these changes have made this year’s Oscar race more unpredictable than ever.

To predict the winners, there are a variety of factors to take into consideration, which we will briefly introduce in the background section. Considering that social media can influence public and private opinions about these nominated movies, in this project, we investigated whether we can use twitter sentiment scores to predict the winners. Since the most talked-about Oscar categories on twitter are Best Picture, Best Actor, Best Actress, Best Supporting Actor and Best Supporting Actress, we will limit our prediction scope to these five main categories.

projects.title: Sentiment Comparison of Political Twitter/Parler Posts prior to the January 6th Insurrection at the Capitol
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Penn State University
projects.description:
The insurrection that took place on January 6th, 2021 is an event that will go down in history as a catastrophic failure by the U.S. government. Heads eventually turned towards Parler, a social media site similar to Twitter as a breeding ground for the extremists to plan their attack on the capitol. Our team compared sentiment scores for Parler and Twitter posts. Posts were gathered from Twitter and Parler prior to January 6th. Separate posts were gathered to train a binary classifier that labels posts as political or non-political. The political posts were then processed to calculate their sentiment scores, and the averages were compared. The average negative sentiment scores for Twitter was higher than Parler for TextBlob, but was lower than Parler for NLTKVader. Average sentiment scores for positive and neutral were relatively similar between TextBlob and NLTKVader. 

Results are inconclusive, with NLTK Vader and TextBlob resulting in different results for average negative sentiment. In future work the classification testing and training sets should be much larger to better classify posts as political or non-political. More finely-tuned methods for sentiment analysis should be used to accurately determine whether negative and positive posts on average were different depending on sentiment analyzer.

projects.description:
In this phase of the semester project our objective was to practice using data science techniques to extract and clean data, and then to integrate data using implementations of some of the techniques we learned in class.

In part A of phase 2 we cleaned the data, identified missing values, and formally assessed the similarity of the data using instance-based matching.

In part B we used FlexMatcher to match columns of different coronavirus datasets together.

honorsAndAwards.title: Bertelsmann Foundation Young Trans-Atlantic Leaders Fellow
honorsAndAwards.description:
The Bertelsmann Foundation, established in 2008, is the North American arm of the Germany-based Bertelsmann Stiftung. Since its inception, the Stiftung has invested more than US$ 1 billion in more than 700 projects. The Stiftung has approximately 300 employees and is headquartered in the northern German town of Gütersloh. It has opened other branches in Brussels and Barcelona. The Washington, DC-based Foundation is part of this network.

The Bertelsmann Foundation is an independent, nonpartisan and nonprofit think tank in Washington with a trans-Atlantic perspective on global challenges. We engage policymakers and thought leaders through innovative projects, research and debate to shape practical recommendations and policy solutions for pressing political, economic and social issues.

The Bertelsmann Foundation established a long-running annual conference that brings together high-level, international representatives of government, business, labor, academia and the media to discuss global cooperation on issues crucial to the future of our societies.

The Bertelsmann Foundation underwrites programs that promote international communication and understanding. We 
1) Bring together US and European officials for exclusive briefings on current and mutual foreign-, economic- and social-policy challenges
2) Established the first fellowship program for Congressional and European Parliament staffers to advance understanding of legislative priorities and processes on both sides of the Atlantic
3) Bring together rising trans-Atlantic leaders and thinkers to explore the common challenges facing the US-European partnership
4) Serve as a facilitator for global dialogue

honorsAndAwards.title: Herbert Scoville Jr. International Security Fellowship
honorsAndAwards.description:
The Herbert Scoville Jr. Peace Fellowship, established in 1987, is a highly-competitive national fellowship program that provides recent college and graduate school alumni with the opportunity to gain a Washington perspective on key issues of peace and security. Twice yearly, the fellowship’s  Board of Directors selects a group of outstanding individuals to spend six to  nine months in Washington. Supported by a salary, the fellows serve as full-time junior staff members at the participating organization of their choice.

The program also arranges meetings for the fellows with policy experts. Many former Scoville Fellows have gone on to pursue graduate degrees in  international relations and related fields and taken prominent positions in the field of peace and security with public-interest organizations, the Federal  Government, academia, and media. To date, 171 fellowships have been awarded.

headline: Director at PwC | Legal Transformation, Information Governance and Privacy Advisor | Data and Information Management Strategist | Non-profit Board Member
about:
Azeem Choudhury is a Director at PwC Advisory.He serves clients within a number of industries, with specific competencies in data management, enterprise content and records management, information governance, legal technology and knowledge management. 

Azeem has over 15 years of experience in helping industry leading organizations, manage their information assets. Azeem has spent a significant amount of time in partnering with leading public and private organizations in implementing and streamlining their business processes in the areas of information management, data governance and records management to enable automation, governance, digital adoption and compliance.

Azeem is an AIIM Certified Information Professional (CIP) and holds specialist certifications in Enterprise Content Management, Electronic Records Management, Microsoft 365 Security, Document Imaging and SCRUM Framework (Certified Scrum Master).

Career Highlights:

· Headed the technical team responsible for the development and implementation of the overall solution architecture for a major retail organization, in support of privacy regulations  
· Spearheaded the analysis and design of a records and document management solution for a major US energy and utility organization. This solution effectively supported mandatory federal and state regulatory compliance requirements. Also, provided leadership for requirements elicitation, design, and development of an enterprise dashboard and reporting solution (Microsoft Power BI and Reporting Services) for operational and leadership teams.
·Headed the design and development of business and functional specifications for a patient engagement mobile application and a provider portal in conjunction with a major pharmaceutical organization. This resulted in an improvement for patient access to medication and overall treatment journey.
·Championed the development of an enterprise content management (ECM) reference architecture for a major US energy and utility organization. This was used as a guideline for all architectural, development, and strategy decisions for managing the company’s structured and semi-structured content going forward.
·Directed efforts in the analysis and development of a document management and business glossary solution for the Enterprise Information Management (EIM) program of a major US state. Ultimately, this enabled the seamless sharing of data across all state agencies.

He has co-developed and commercialized multiple revenue-generating solutions with an annual pipeline of over US$50m, such as Electric Vehicles, Storage technologies, and Energy reforms, by setting up and driving the Project Management Office (PMO), defining the roadmap, KPIs, managing sales, and client activation. 

Shikhar is also a startup mentor and associated with multiple incubation centres. He is a thought leader in the market and publishes points of view across energy and mobility-related themes. experience.companyName: Co-authored an article in the International Journal of Aging and Human Development
experience.description:
• Co-authored an article in the International Journal of Aging and Human Development using a randomized experiment that replicated and extended previous experimental work with older adults (Smith & Bryant, 2019) by testing potential mediating variables through which savoring valuable “life lessons” improved attitudes toward aging and boosts psychological well- being.
• Conducted multiple bootstrap analyses which revealed, compared to the control condition, reflecting on life lessons produced stronger feelings of gratitude (but not stronger, general positive affect), which in turn boosted positive attitudes toward aging, life satisfaction, state hope, and state self-esteem.
• Supported an integrative, three-path meditational model, in which reflecting on life lessons increased reported levels of savoring, which in turn led to greater gratitude, which was associated with heightened positive attitudes toward aging, life satisfaction, and state hope.

A long-tenured M&A advisor with the tenacity and potent ability to get to the heart of the matter in the complex world of dealmaking, known as an innovative and strategic leader in the field.  Whether advising corporate or private equity clients through acquisitions, divestitures, joint ventures or navigating the flow and tension that each deal presents, my clients highly value the clarity and focus I bring to the inherent uncertainty of M&A.  

I thrive on the complexity a deal presents and tackle it with unwavering curiosity and perseverance.  Just as I excel as a chef in the kitchen, I incorporate my experiences to create optimal outcomes for clients.  Empowering others and giving back is an integral part of my life – I  channel my leadership talents to forward economic empowerment in his community.

experience.position: Partner | U.S. Deals Clients & Markets Leader
experience.description:
An experienced M&A professional, working with executives in both buy-side and sell-side transactions to help clients make informed and empowered investment, divestment, capital market and reorganization decisions.  My commercial acumen and focus on value enables a persistent defining of the "can be" potential of a transaction, built on knowledge and actionable business levers.   

An outstanding client track record is heightened by my active involvement in shaping the strategic direction and thought leadership of the PwC Deals practice and teaming with my colleagues and the community to produce exceptional results from leading our industry-focused deal teams, delivering sector-experienced professionals who benefit from extensive knowledge in the industry to bringing our client's the credentials and insight from doing more deals than any other firm.   

My teams work with clients at any point in their journey to uncover opportunities using the latest in cutting-edge technology and proprietary data analytics tools, delivering the insights needed to make the right decision at the right time.   Not only do we focus on understanding the risks in transactions, but also the opportunities and ways to harness them.

As a Director, my return to the US focused on my interest and passion for transactions.  Working with Corporate and Private Equity clients, and teaming with partners and professional across our Firm, I assisted executives in both buy-side and sell-side due diligence, enabling valuation and investment decisions.  
• Assessed and communicated financial, economic, tax, human resource and technology impacts of transactions, and supporting negotiations impacting client investment and capital requirements. 
• Facilitated client preparation for financing and advised on investment structuring and complex accounting issues.  
• As the Great Recession arrived, I was also fortunate to spend time working with distressed businesses as the navigated the economic headwinds.

Promoted to Manager shortly after arriving in the UK, I spent three years working across eastern and western Europe, assisting European multinationals on cross border M&A as well as capital raising during all stages of the SEC registration and listing process.  
•  Advised senior management, attorneys and investment bankers on the process to raise equity and debt and the registration process including offering memorandums, SEC comment letters, and comfort letters.
•  Advised US clients on cross border acquisitions throughout Europe.
•  This role was where my interest in M&A, and passion for the dynamic world of deal making, took shape.

I began my career in Chicago, as an audit intern and then Associate.  My early clients included both privately held and public listed companies, from manufacturing to consumer products, from services  to medical device and diagnostics.  I was promoted quickly from Associate, to Senior Associate, and then tranferred to London in my first three years with PwC.

publications.title: M&A breathes new life into brand portfolios for spirits companies
publications.description: 2021 is ripe for deals in the spirits sector. In 2020, shelter-in-place mandates depressed sales of alcohol in restaurants and bars, while home consumption ticked up.  In the wake of the pandemic, many states also revised laws to permit bars and restaurants to sell alcohol to go.   Consumer trends already in place— including a shift to premium brands, ready-to-drink (RTD) products and direct-to-consumer (DTC) business models — accelerated over the course of 2020. PwC's own Emerging Consumer Sentiment research has found that among other changes, consumers were willing to try new brands.

publications.title: Consumer sector M&A poised to rebound after 2020 slump
publications.description: Large consumer companies armed with big cash stockpiles could propel a surge in M&A over the next 12 months as favorable monetary and fiscal policies and vaccine deployments increase the likelihood of an economic recovery.  Consumer deal-making was markedly weaker in 2020 as lockdown restrictions and the economic slowdown hit the sector especially hard. The number of consumer deals fell 15.6% to 5,029 in 2020 from 5,957 in 2019, while the value of transactions plunged 43.1% to $199.92 billion from $351.29 billion over the same period, according to data compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence.

publications.title: Consumer markets deals insights: 2021 outlook
publications.description:
M&A investments focus on strengthening core operations, building operational efficiencies, and expanding digital capabilities to build resilience and emerge stronger in the post-COVID new-normal.
The COVID-19 pandemic has changed consumer behavior and disrupted the competitive landscape of Consumer Markets. In response, companies have accelerated their operational strategies and embraced digital transformation, resulting in ample M&A opportunities.

publications.title: 2021 outlook: M&A leads the economic recovery
publications.description:
The M&A recovery that began in the second half of 2020 will accelerate in 2021, as corporate and private investors have access to capital and can pursue deals to build scale and expand scope.
For some, growth will come within industries, with market leaders strengthening their position as the economy continues to recover. Others, seeing their business models upended by the COVID-19 pandemic, will explore how small or medium-sized bets in adjacent sectors can help drive transformation. And M&A targets will come from a growing pool of sellers — businesses that have fallen into distress during the recession, private investors that always think about holding periods and exits, and companies that are reassessing strategies and could part with non-core assets, especially as valuations remain high.

publications.title: RETAIL GETS REAL PODCAST How COVID-19 is changing mergers and acquisitions
publications.description: Fundamental shifts in retail have created “not just new ways of shopping,” says John Potter, U.S. Deals Partner at PwC — they’ve also created “new ways of being.” Potter, who advises corporate and private equity clients as they buy and sell businesses, joined this week’s Retail Gets Real podcast to discuss mergers and acquisitions, how the effects of the pandemic have shifted business strategies, and opportunities for investments in retail.

publications.title: Succeeding through M&A in uncertain economic times
publications.description: The capital available for deals usually dries up during a downturn. This time will likely be different, with companies better able to explore inorganic growth.

publications.title: Retailers Cut Transformative Deals
publications.description: Consumer markets just experienced a record-breaking year for deal making in terms of total deal value and volume. While that activity paints a positive economic outlook for the retail industry, what is more telling — and even inspiring — is some of retail’s deals surrounding analytics, tech, and artificial intelligence (AI). These deals are rooted in the need for retailers to quickly change with their customers as part of the Retail Evolution or risk falling behind. These particular acquisitions can help dealmakers build their analytical power, adopt emerging technologies and integrate AI into both operations and the customer experience.

publications.title: An Appetite for M&A: How Food Companies Can Buy and Sell Their Way to Competitive Advantage
publications.description: Faced with new and challenging market forces, food companies are changing their strategic approach by focusing on capabilities to drive how they organize and operate their businesses. For winning companies, this focus on capabilities is informing their growth path, including their approach mergers, acquisitions, and divestitures.

publications.title: Spotlight article on How Food Companies Can Buy and Sell Their Way to Competitive Advantage, plus our Retail and Consumer Deals Insights – 2014/15
publications.description: Highlights consumer sentiment continued its upward trend in 2014 due to more favorable prospects for the domestic economy. Core retail trade sales have improved as wages are increasing, unemployment is at a low and fuel prices have fallen, but at an unimpressive rate. Although retailers that cater to consumers in the lower- and middle-income categories may benefit disproportionately from the decline in fuel prices because their customers spend a higher portion of their discretionary income on gasoline, organic growth may remain a challenge for businesses. While the impact will vary across different retail demographics and channels, we anticipate that companies will continue to engage in deals to drive growth and reposition their businesses.

publications.title: Fast-tracking alliances to create new value
publications.description: CEOs affirm that the recent revival in corporate deals is poised to continue in 2015.  The survey also revealed that the nature of deals in 2015 is changing, with companies looking to other industries as potential targets—or potential competitors. More than half of CEOs globally think it likely that their companies will increasingly compete in new sectors over the next three years. And what they’re after is also changing, with more CEOs looking for access to new technology and customers, as much as markets.

publications.title: US CEOs more open to business alliances, ways to work together
publications.description: Alliances are becoming core to strategy in a time when innovation capacity will determine future growth prospects and even relevance for many of today’s mainstream business. Yet intent is one thing, ability to come through with a successful alliance that goes beyond a traditional JV is another. Learn what US CEOs told us in our 2014 US CEO Survey.

publications.title: 2014 M&A Outlook
publications.description:
Positive M&A Momentum in Second Half of 2013 to Carry into 2014, as disciplined planning and execution support range of deal options in marketplace and favorable debt and equity markets drive increased opportunities for deals, capital raising and financing.

Strong momentum in the merger and acquisition (M&A) market during the second half of 2013 is expected to continue into 2014, according to PwC US.  Improved stability and early signs of growth in other key global markets have contributed to an increasing level of business confidence and sharpening focus on finding opportunities for growth, setting the stage for positive M&A momentum.

publications.title: A Vision for M&A: Best Practices for Creating a Winning Acquisition Strategy
publications.description: Chapter Five contributor....Drawing on the experience and expertise of the ‘best in class’ dealmakers, The M&A Advisor, together with Merrill Datasite, is publishing a dealmakers guide series – The Best Practices of The Best Dealmakers. This fifth chapter: “A Vision for M&A: Best Practices for Creating a Winning Acquisition Strategy” outlines the best practices for developing an effective acquisition plan as part of the overall corporate growth strategy.

publications.title: PwC US retail & consumer deals insights: Q2 2013
publications.description: Despite a lull in deal activity during Q2, M&A fundamentals remain strong with corporate cash availability, a favorable debt environment and continued private equity sponsor interest. Retail remains attractive for investment, particularly as businesses seek greater effi ciencies with scale as well as international expansion. Private equity activity in retail remained strong, comprising two of the top deals during the quarter.

publications.title: 2013 Midyear M&A Outlook
publications.description: Quality execution trumps volume as M&A levels remain restrained.... CEOs are bullish with at least 75 percent expecting growth over the next year through both organic means and acquisitions.  Nearly half of U.S. CEOs said they plan to do a deal in 2013, indicating that dealmaking remains top of mind for business leaders, however, less than one third of those U.S. CEOs seeking a deal completed one in the preceding 12 months.  This shift in frequency – and the pace of individual deal participants – is one factor impacting how deals are being executed in today’s increasingly competitive market.  With readily available financing, corporate cash levels at $1.29 trillion, and strong equity markets, PwC expects the combination of these critical factors to support sustained deal activity through the remainder of 2013

BRM Stock Aggregator and Future Return Predictor macro will take 5 stocks and generate 5 years of each stock’s historical data. Chicago United's mission is to to achieve parity in economic opportunity for people of color by advancing multiracial leadership in corporate governance, expanding the talent pipeline for executive-level management, and growing minority businesses.  Chicago United's vision is a Chicago region that is the most inclusive business ecosystem in the nation.

Start Early was founded in 1982 as the Ounce of Prevention Fund, a nonprofit public-private partnership. Since the beginning, Start Early has delivered best-in-class doula, home visiting and Early Head Start and Head Start programs and advocated for thoughtful policies and adequate funding at the local, state, and federal levels. From their roots directly serving families and children on Chicago’s South Side and rural Illinois, they have expanded nationwide impacting early childhood programs and policies with partnerships in 25 states. Their role as on-the-ground practitioners continues to be the bedrock of their expertise and source of innovation and leadership in the field.

Start Early's story is focused on the idea that starting early and nurturing the attachments between children and adults are essential to a child’s present and future well-being. Decades of research have proven that quality early childhood programs are a smart investment. Start Early's founder, businessman and philanthropist Irving B. Harris, understood that the best hope for leveling the playing field and allowing children to thrive is to invest in the earliest days and create intensive, long-term support for a developing child and their family.

The Executives’ Club of Chicago is the premier resource for connecting, developing, and growing best-in-class leaders to strengthen themselves and their organizations. It provides established and emerging leaders opportunities to develop and nurture meaningful relationships, participate in innovative programming, and gain world-class knowledge to expand their perspectives and sharpen their capabilities.

Through cutting edge thought leadership, leadership development and mentoring initiatives, and member experiences, Exec Club brings together business, civic and academic leaders from all industries to discuss issues and opportunities affecting business in Chicago and the world.

Kids First Chicago’s mission is to dramatically improve education for Chicago’s children by ensuring their families are respected authorities and decision-makers in their children’s education. K1C partners with families to help them gain the resources, information, access, and voice they need to achieve their vision for their children.

K1C believes that a healthy education environment where kids, schools, and communities thrive is the key to a world-class city. They believe that those closest to our students - families, community members, and educators - are best equipped to design policies and systems that will improve equity and lead to stronger outcomes for our students, our communities, and our city.

While their work benefits all of Chicago, they strategically focus a large portion of our parent engagement in the city’s West and South Side communities, where historical disinvestment has left far too many Black and Latinx/a/o parents out of the conversation for far too long.
The mission of the Illinois Chamber of Commerce is to be the unifying leader of policies that support growth in Illinois’ dynamic and diverse economy.

World Business Chicago cultivates relationships across all of our city’s dynamic industries. WBC's mission is to drive inclusive economic growth and job creation, support businesses, and promote Chicago as the leading global city to help our existing companies expand as well as attract new companies.  WBC's vision is to make Chicago the most business-friendly city in the world by becoming a role model for truly inclusive economic growth, ensuring that all Chicagoans prosper through equitable economic development.

Chicago International Charter School (CICS) was founded on the belief that every child has the right to a high quality education. The mission of Chicago International is to provide, through innovation and choice, an attractive and rigorous college-preparatory education that meets the needs of today’s students.  CICS expects the best of every student and, in turn, provides the support each student needs to achieve their best.

This belief and vision set by our founding Board in 1997, has led to Chicago International becoming the largest charter school operator in Illinois and a frontrunner in thought leadership in the school reform movement. CICS now operates a network of 16 campuses across the cities of Chicago, and Rockford, serving 9,200 students in K through 12th grade.

CICS believes that all young people can achieve, when given the right support. This philosophy has led to significant academic results. CICS is proud to share that, in CICS elementary school campuses that have been opened for three or more years, CICS has closed the achievement gap between CICS students (88% of whom qualify for free/reduced lunch and 96% of whom are African American or Hispanic/Latino) and a national sample of students in grades 1st through 8th in reading and grades 1st through 4th and 6th through 8th in math.

headline: Strategy Consulting & Advisory | International Growth Practice
about:
Jaron is a skilled strategy advisor with a diverse background in business and technology. He has worked with clients internationally in Germany and China, offering innovative solutions to complex business challenges and helping them achieve their goals. Jaron excels at synthesizing market insights, driving digital transformation, and analyzing new products for market entry, and his proposals have consistently received approval from senior stakeholders.

Before his career in management consulting, Jaron co-founded three start-ups in various industries, including electric bikes, robotics, and product design. He has also been recognized with multiple innovation awards and holds a co-authorship on a US design patent. With a strong foundation in science and technology and a broad understanding of the humanities, arts, and social sciences, Jaron has a unique ability to lead in technical and design matters.

Outside of work, Jaron serves as a venture advisor and mentor to undergraduate students, helping them navigate their careers and pursue entrepreneurial endeavours. He is always open to connecting over coffee or a glass of wine and can be reached at jaronleejw@gmail.com. His key areas of expertise include strategic management, digital transformation, change management, project ownership and management, stakeholder management, people management, venture building and assessment, intercultural communication, creative thinking, and design thinking.

projects.title: Optimising the effects of Vertical Wind Harvester using Aerodynamic Principles
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)
projects.description:
Wind energy is one of the best sources of renewable alternative energy. Since it’s renewable, it does not produce any harmful pollutants or emissions during operation that would harm the environment. We decided to build a Vertical Axis Wind Harvester as it has the following advantages over the traditional Horizontal Axis Wind Harvesters.

1)       By strategically selecting and positioning the blades, the product is able to harvest winds at lower speeds.

2)       It is effective at areas with a low height restriction as its size can be reduced and compact such that when assembled together it was able to provide an efficient area to power ratio.

3)       It is Omni-directional which does not require the user to track the direction of oncoming winds. This increases efficiency as it eliminates the complex mechanism required to move the traditional horizontal wind harvesters to face the oncoming wind.

4)       Lower maintenance cost as the wind harvester sits on the ground rather than high up in the air.

5)       Lesser fatigue as compared to horizontal wind harvesters as concepts of aerodynamics was utilised to reduce blades fatigue and vibration.

projects.title: Salamander - Portable Amphibious Spherical Rolling Robot with Live-Streaming Capability for Ground and Aquatic Deployment
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)
projects.description: Abstract: Forested terrains and mudflats surrounded by water bodies such as rivers, lakes, and swamps are difficult to maneuver around, especially for man-made automations and robots. The lack of reliable robotic platforms often hinders operations such as search-and-rescue, surveillance, and research efforts made in these terrains. Whereas most developments are focused on improving maneuverability on either land or water, little has been done in developing robotic platforms with amphibious capability. To address this design gap, an amphibious spherical rolling robot design is proposed. A spherical rolling robot is advantageous in terms of its self-righting capability, balancing capability, and minimum damage to the surrounding during its mobilization. The proposed design contains a battery-powered fixed two-axis pendulum for the robots powertrain, which provides the robot with its self-righting capability. Two modular live-feed cameras are inserted to provide live-streaming capability, both of which can be easily replaced with other relevant sensors if needed. A custom-made 3D-printed sleeve is designed to improve the robot’s propulsion on both land and water. Most of the robot’s design features are highly modular, facilitating customization depending on the user’s needs. With these configurations, the final prototype exhibited a high degree of maneuverability on both land and water. The live-streaming capability was proven with a video recording from the robot’s cameras when deployed.

headline: purpose visionary| c-suite executive| board director| sustainability specialist |social impact expert| leader advisor| skilled speaker| retired PwC partner-Chief Purpose Officer
about:
Shannon Schuyler is a pioneering strategist at the intersection of purpose and performance. As PwC's US Chief Purpose & Inclusion Officer, Shannon leveraged her 30yrs of experience transforming how organizations drive sustainable success through cultural innovation and strategic purpose alignment. She architected frameworks proving how a purpose-driven culture catalyzes business value and market leadership.     

Her unique approach intentionally integrates strategy and culture. Shannon's global leadership across PwC's US, Mexico, Asia-Pacific US Territories and 8 international centers prove that organizations perform better when purpose and culture are strategically aligned. As the US and Mexico Climate Risk Leader, she highlighted how embedding purpose into core strategy fosters resilience and competitive advantage.    

Shannon also brought focus to the role PwC plays in our communities.  With responsible business leadership as the bedrock, she led efforts to harness the power of the business and the skills of our people to respond to systemic challenges which create disparity across society.  PwCers have the opportunity to fuel their purpose by using their skills in service of their communities and causes that they are passionate about. At the core of this work were the firm’s first multi-year community commitments focused on financial literacy, digital acumen and investing in a charitable foundation that grew from infancy to an over $200M giving entity.     

Her pioneering work extends beyond traditional metrics. Under her guidance, PwC emerged as a case study in driving shareholder value and societal impact. At CEO Action for Diversity & Inclusion™, Shannon helped transform a business commitment into the largest CEO-driven movement of its kind, engaging over 2,400 organizations. This led her to promote innovation and enhance business value by connecting purpose with belonging, fostering an environment that celebrates identity and intersectionality.   

Having catalyzed transformative change throughout her career, Shannon is energized to take on her next challenge, bringing her unique expertise in purpose-driven strategy and cultural transformation to new frontiers. Based in Chicago, where she lives with her husband and son, Shannon's influence continues to grow as more organizations recognize that culture, purpose, and strategy must work in concert to drive lasting organizational success.

slides.title: Purpose Trends Shaping 2023: It’s No Longer a Journey
slides.subtitle: Shannon Schuyler-Sustainable Impact and Culture Strategist on LinkedIn
slides.description: Great things lie ahead. It’s what I’ve concluded as I reflect on the year behind us. But those things will only come if we collectively continue to take action. Over the past year, purpose has played a pivotal role in shaping the “why” behind what organizations, large and small, do. That role will only grow stronger. Here’s how I see it evolving in 2023. DEI is no longer a journey. We can no longer say we’re journeying toward diversity, equity and inclusion. We can’t say we’re journeying toward social change or climate equity either. We need to set tangible, measurable goals and execute strategies that have clear timelines, just as we would any other business priority, and strive to meet our purpose. Now is the moment to hold ourselves accountable and put true grit into how we deliver sustainable impact, because purpose and inclusion can be measured. And it should be. We should set aspirational goals and use the data as a starting point, not an end unto itself. When we do this, our actions are tied to business outcomes, something that’s critically important, especially in times of economic uncertainty. Purpose is a deciding factor for talent. There's no doubt that talent dynamics have shifted over the past few years -- and that organizations are fundamentally changed because of it. In the competitive landscape for attracting and retaining talent, talent has won and while economic downturns have impacted that balance, the effect will only be temporary. We’ve arrived at a point where we need to reimagine career paths to help drive a more personalized experience and putting purpose at the forefront of that is key. Being a responsible company is table stakes. This year, we should give people the space to not only find their personal purpose but activate it through purpose projects that connect the content of their jobs and broader meaning in their lives. There are no more sidelines. From the board to the C-suite, business leaders will continue to be confronted with issues that they will be uncomfortable discussing. But they are topics that matter to the diverse group of stakeholders, which has broadened immensely over the past few years, that each organization has. Leaders can no longer stay silent. While they won’t need to lean into every societal issue, they should use their purpose to dictate when and why they take action or not. Getting comfortable with being uncomfortable will take resiliency, but if societal issues are left unaddressed, trust among key stakeholder groups can be jeopardized and damage organizational reputation and value. To be clear, purpose will continue to be at the forefront of driving sustainable change in business throughout 2023. And our purpose to build trust in society and solve important problems will continue to guide us here at PwC. Purpose is a North Star for business leaders to guide their strategy, actions, commitments and culture and is what stakeholders align to. Purpose paired with values will make an organization distinctive and sustainable. And to capitalize on the momentum from 2022, we need to continue to come together versus going it alone – we must lean into purpose.

headline: Global Indirect Tax Senior Associate at PwC Chicago
about:
Motivated recent graduate and licensed CPA from the University of Puerto Rico in Ponce, majoring in Accounting with a minor in Finance. 

During my school years, I worked as the Accounting Tutor for my campus, participated in an internship opportunity for a global professional services firm, volunteered, researched, and performed as a board member of a Student Association. All those different roles allowed me to develop as a leader, creating solid relationships with my peers and mentors that motivate me to continue learning and advancing my career goals. One of my fondest memories from my academic experience was the opportunity to collaborate in a research project on Accounting Outsourcing, which I got to present at my Institution's Student Research and Creation Congress.

experience.position: Global Indirect Tax (VAT/GST) Consulting Senior Associate

experience.companyName: Academic Support Center for Students and Faculty
experience.description:
As an Accounting Tutor, I got to contribute to the student's learning process by: 
Preparing lesson material and additional practice to assist in the development of technical financial reporting skills.
Creating visualizations, research, and lectures for their Principles of Accounting Course Materials.
Leading test material reviews with study groups from various disciplines. 
Acting as a mentor for Freshman and Sophomore students on Internship search, course selection, and college life advice.

As a second-year Indirect Tax Practice Intern, I got the opportunity to work alongside the Chicago Value Added Tax Practice, which allowed me to:
Collaborate in cross-functional teams assisting clients with Tax Compliance and Reporting issues. 
Assist in ERP System implementations for Global Supply Chains with their corresponding Tax Implications.  
Participate in team training on Global Tax Developments focusing on Value Added Tax.
Develop my technical Global Tax Knowledge, Terminology, and professional client service soft skills.

Volunteering with the IRS during a Tax Season under the VITA program allowed me to:
Complete Basic Tax Certification Training along with certifications in Ethics, Interviews, and Puerto Rico-specific Federal Tax implications. 
Perform taxpayer interviews on income, dependents, expenses, and household information for tax credits assessment, and return preparation. 
Answer taxpayers' questions on tax issues, including the new Child Tax Credit requirements. 
Use IRS's TAX PRO software to directly prepare, review, and submit filers' returns. 
Collaborate on the centers' planning including scheduling, document filing, and report preparations.

During my first year as an Advanced Tax Intern with the Indirect Tax Practice, I joined the Income and Franchise team, which allowed me to:
Perform research on Apportionments, Nexus, Amendments, and Consolidations in US State and Local Tax jurisdictions.  
Modify, Review, and Export finalized Corporate Tax Returns for State Agency Submittal for Medical, Services, and Telecommunication industries.
Assist the firm’s leadership with administrative tasks like billing, document filing, and attending client-facing meetings, allowing me to develop my online client service skills.

As a Start Intern, I got to experience what a career in public accounting could turn into by:
Participating in professional presence, leadership, and excel training.
Exploring data manipulation, analytics, and visualization software like Tableau, Alteryx, and PowerBI.
Networking with other interns from all over the country and with PwC professionals from different role levels and lines of service.
Developing and using my skills and firm resources while participating in a Skills of Society Group Project in which we helped a Nonprofit Organization achieve its goals and solve its problems.
Explore the different lines of service, inclusion networks, and solutions provided to clients by experiencing simulations of both the firm's Audit and Tax practices.

His range of experiences span asset development and Health Authority interactions to global regulatory functional strategy and management.  Mike is currently a Director in the Health Industries Risk & Regulatory advisory team for PwC based in Chicago.

His areas of expertise include:  Regulatory strategy, Health Authority engagement, global operating model design, core capability development, technology enablement, and digital disruption.  Prior to joining PwC Mike was a Regulatory Liaison focusing in Cardiovascular and Metabolic compounds ranging from Phase I – IV in addition to post-doctoral experiences within academia and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

Mike holds a Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) degree from Butler University and a Masters of Business Administration from the Tobin College of Business at St. John’s University.  Mike also completed a 2 year post-doctoral program in Regulatory Strategy.

topSkills: ServiceNow • Project Management • Business Analysis Planning & Monitoring • Generative AI • Stakeholder Management
about:
As a seasoned Business Analyst and Project Manager with a proven track record in ServiceNow implementations (ITSM, FSM, CSM), I specialize in bridging the gap between technology and operational teams to streamline processes and improve service delivery. My background spans multiple industries, including telecommunications, 5G network optimization, and healthcare, where I've consistently delivered innovative solutions that drive efficiency and enhance customer satisfaction.

At Boost Mobile, I led the redesign of key ServiceNow modules, collaborating with cross-functional teams to define over 300 requirements and optimize workflows across Incident Management, Work Orders, and Change Management. My work contributed to the overall enhancement of Boost’s 5G network, ensuring quicker resolution of site-related issues and greater user satisfaction. Additionally, I championed the adoption of Generative AI to automate workflows and support data-driven decision-making, positioning the company for a competitive advantage in 2025.

In my time at Epic Systems, I directed IT projects to implement Epic Software across multiple hospitals, focusing on custom design validations and task management that ultimately improved patient care. My experience includes working with medical leadership, providing training, and enhancing system integration, which directly impacted operational efficiency and patient safety.

I bring strong expertise in requirements gathering, data analysis, process mapping, and stakeholder management, and I thrive in environments where complex problem-solving and cross-functional collaboration are critical to success. Passionate about continuous learning, I am dedicated to improving operational outcomes and guiding teams toward industry best practices, including ServiceNow certifications for internal teams.

experience.description:
Led the onboarding of Delta Airlines onto ServiceNow, as they transitioned off Salesforce, gathering 100+ requirements and translating aviation, safety, and compliance needs into scalable workflows, dashboards, and data models aligned with Delta’s Business Process Expectations.

Designed and implemented a custom Aviation Case Management solution supporting aircraft maintenance, flight operations, safety reporting, compliance reviews, and RMA processes, projected to reduce manual data entry by 60% and cut cross-team handoff delays by 40%.

Developed detailed solution design documentation, workflow maps, and integration specifications for maintenance, compliance, and operations teams, ensuring scalable architecture capable of supporting 20,000+ monthly aviation cases.

Partnered with cross-functional engineering, safety, and compliance leads to customize case lifecycle stages, approval flows, and escalation rules, enabling proactive tracking of flight-critical issues and projected to reduce audit-related backlog by 45%.

Coordinated UAT planning, test scripts, and feedback loops with Hughes stakeholders and Delta operations teams to prepare the aviation solution for enterprise-wide deployment.

experience.position: Business Analyst II (ServiceNow - Cell Site Operations)
experience.description:
Led the redesign of IT Service Management (ITSM) and Field Service Management (FSM) modules of ServiceNow, enabling operational teams to capture detailed and relevant information, resulting in 65% faster resolution time and reducing escalations by 40%.

Collaborated with cross-functional teams to gather and define over 400 requirements, documented the respective solution designs, and managed the delivery and optimization of ServiceNow’s Incident, Work Order, Work Order Task, Change, Case Forms, and Problem Forms — driving a 30% improvement in SLA compliance and contributing to the stability of Boost Mobile’s 5G Network.

Established the Problem Management module in ServiceNow, developing processes to identify recurring incidents, conducting root-cause analysis, and implementing long-term solutions that reduced repeated outages by 25% and cut high-severity incident frequency by 140 per month.

Designed and launched the Case Management module, partnering with customer support teams to improve case intake, routing, and escalation processes — reducing case backlog by 35% and decreasing average resolution time from 72 hours to 4 hours.

Led the rollout of Purchase Order (PO) Automation in ServiceNow, enabling Field Engineers to request third-party resources through automated workflows that enforced legal, financial, and compliance guidelines — reducing PO processing time from 14 days to 1 day and ensuring 100% audit compliance

Conducted over 50+ workflow process demos for end users on the effective use of ServiceNow modules to optimize tracking of site-related issues impacting the 5G network — resulting in a 87% increase in user adoption and a measurable rise in satisfaction survey results

Directed and coordinated an IT project team to implement Epic Software across 14 University Hospitals in Cleveland (UH Cleveland) through custom design validations, task management, and data-driven analysis — improving patient care delivery and achieving a 23% reduction in documentation errors.

Implemented the Cupid-Cardiology Application, overseeing revenue management, third-party interface integration, and training initiatives across multiple hospital enterprises — increasing billing accuracy by 12% and enhancing operational efficiency by 58 hours saved.

Successfully installed PeopleSoft Supply Chain Management at UH Cleveland, streamlining the tracking and management of medical supplies — ensuring 100% compliance with revenue reporting standards.

Collaborated with hospital medical leadership to define installation scope, develop mitigation plans, and deliver monthly progress reports — resulting in a 26% improvement in customer satisfaction and measurable gains in operational engagement.

Provided cardiology workflow training to physicians, nurses, and medical personnel at UH Cleveland, Baptist Health (Arkansas), Central East Hospital (Toronto), and New York Consortium — training over 200+ clinicians, boosting end-user adoption by 75%, and ensuring reliable software use that enhanced patient safety.

Designed and developed an Echo Synopsis Activity, enabling physicians worldwide to track patients’ longitudinal data — improving long-term patient monitoring and supporting evidence-based clinical decision-making, adopted by 5+ hospitals within the first year.

publications.title: Networking human biomarker and hazardous chemical elements from building materials: Systematic literature review and in vivo test
publications.description: Healthy and comfortable indoor environment has attracted attentions by researchers as people spend majority of time inside enclosed spaces. Details regarding hazardous chemicals emanated from those are not systemically investigated and managed despite the significance of building materials that consists in indoor space. Furthermore, it is well known that specific materials are believed to have lessen or have negative health effect. Therefore, it is necessary to explore the health impact caused by building material and relative hazardous chemicals. In this study, analysis of literature and standards on hazardous chemicals within the field of indoor environment and related health outcomes that focuses on building materials was conducted. Moreover, preliminary in vivo test on small scale animals follows thereafter in order to prove the existence of link between biomarker and building materials e.g. dermatology. It was found that building materials had an impact on Atopic Dermatitis (AD) where 10% and 20% of diatomite board showed a positive impact compared to gypsum board, which showed a negative impact. The results were developed as a framework for networking building materials, relevant chemical elements and potential biomarker indicating positive or negative biological impact. Accumulated data on biomarker based on epidemiological surveillance and in vivo tests will contribute to building a repository to guide potential harmfulness and healing impact of building materials.

experience.description:
I lead strategic initiatives at the intersection of artificial intelligence, data governance, and public policy for the Government of Rajasthan — driving the State’s vision to become a national pioneer in responsible and proactive AI-led governance.

My work spans the design and execution of the Rajasthan AI Policy 2025–30 and the SMART (Service Management with AI/ML & Real-Time System) Project, both aimed at institutionalising AI adoption across departments for citizen-centric outcomes.

Key Leadership Contributions:
• Spearheading Rajasthan’s AI Policy, shaping the State’s roadmap for inclusive, ethical, and scalable AI integration across governance, research, skilling, and industry enablement.

• Leading the SMART Project, a flagship data-driven governance platform that creates a unified data lake and enables 360° beneficiary profiling across government schemes and services.
• Championing the use of AI for proactive welfare delivery, where non-financial benefits are automatically triggered based on citizen data patterns—setting a benchmark for anticipatory governance in India.
• Building institutional frameworks for data interoperability, privacy assurance, and AI ethics in alignment with national standards and the Digital India framework.
• Collaborating with senior government leadership, technology partners, and policy experts to accelerate digital transformation and strengthen the AI innovation ecosystem in Rajasthan.

Through these initiatives, I am working to position Rajasthan as a model state for AI governance, where technology is leveraged not merely for efficiency, but for empowerment, inclusion, and foresight-driven decision-making.

Advisor to Rajasthan Government - Financial Policy, Public-Private Collaborations, and Digital Transformation

In my advisory role with the Rajasthan government, I focus on evaluating the financial implications of key policies and budget announcements, providing insights to ensure effective and sustainable economic planning.

I also play a key role in driving public-private collaborations across several sectors, with a focus on digital transformation, including:

	•	Skill Development: Supporting initiatives that leverage technology to enhance workforce skills and align them with industry requirements.
	•	Fund of Funds for Startups: Assisting in the design of investment frameworks aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship through digital platforms.
	•	Employment Exchange Platform: Leading efforts to create a modern, digital employment ecosystem that connects job seekers with employers more efficiently.

By integrating digital transformation into these projects, I strive to contribute to Rajasthan’s long-term socio-economic growth and innovation.

In order to boost the e-government endeavors at all levels of governance and also to embark on the journey for Digital Government excellence, National e-Governance Service Delivery Assessment (NeSDA) initiative has been undertaken by Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DAPRG), Govt. of India.
NeSDA framework, launched in August 2018, was conceptualized with an overall objective to measure the depth and effectiveness of existing e-Governance service delivery mechanisms. This framework, based on the Online Service Index (OSI) of UNDESA eGovernment Survey, has been customized for the Indian federal structure and the e-Governance landscape of the States and UTs. NeSDA is first of its kind initiative in India.
The first edition of the biennial study - National e-Governance Service Delivery Assessment 2019 was released during February 2020.

Responsibilities assigned during NeSDA 2023:
1. Baselining online service delivery of e-Government in India
2. Benchmarking the online service delivery from other countries in EGDI scoring
3. The framework for NeSDA 2023 study has been elaborated under the following three dimensions.
-Portals Coverage: State portal, City portal and Services portal
-Mandatory Services Coverage: 59 services for each State across India
-Assessment Parameters: 10 parameters 
4.Assessment portal was developed with workflow functionalities
5. Citizen Survey was developed. The purpose of this survey is to gain insight on the citizens' experience in availing e-services from their respective States/UTs.
6. Data analysis and visualisation of the data collected through assessment.
7. Preparing scoring and benchmarking report for all the 36 States/UTs of India.

a. People Knowledge and Behavior: Building this framework involved several people related changes. It is critical that a knowledge network is set up and resources are identified. A successful framework drives behavioral change, infuse knowledge sharing in the culture.

b. Content Building and dissemination: This included assessing the knowledge needs aligning it with the strategic knowledge areas. Quality of the content, was made integral for successful knowledge dissemination.

c. Governance and Process: Operational processes, procedures, guidelines for data
collection, management, storage were essentially included. They are the foundation of any knowledge management platform. Data Integrity, Security, Privacy are cornerstones of compliance and regulation framework.

d. Digital Enablement: The framework will go a long way in providing convenience, ease of access. Technical tools and capabilities will enable knowledge seekers to get access to structured information and there by simplify their search.

about:

He is currently a Senior Manager at PwC focusing on architecture, design, build and operations of cloud security solutions for his clients, with expertise in data protection and privacy domains. During his career as a cybersecurity consultant, he assisted, managed, and led several projects as part of his clients’ technology transformation and application modernization journey. Additionally, his Subject Matter Speciality as it relates to delivering client engagement includes the following areas - sensitive data scanning and discovery in cloud applications, data loss prevention (and CASB), data encryption, encryption keys and certificate management

about:
As a bilingual tri-national, I am naturally drawn to appreciate the value of diversity in all forms. This is why I have assured that my work and life experience be as eclectic and diversified as possible! 

Education-wise, I graduated top 1% of my cohort with a BBA in Finance and Summa Cum Laude distinction. I am also grateful to have received a multitude of awards and a scholarship worth $100k. 
Professionally, I have contributed highly in my 2.5+ years with two of the largest Big Four financial services firms. My experience of 30+ client-facing projects across a multitude of diverse industries has shaped me into an always-learning, always-adapting individual. From the subjectivity of client communications and presentations and managing my junior team to the more analytical conduction of DCF and market approach valuations, I have found the sweet spot of contributing my professional skillset and personality to any environment I'm placed in.

My experience is not limited to the finance field, however! Midaus, WarmItUp, and TrashTalk are three of my initiatives tackling issues like public speaking fears, the inconvenience of cold tea, and littering in the Middle East. I am also learning French, Russian, and American Sign Language to expand my opportunities for societal contribution (and sometimes just for fun!).

experience.description:
•	Received appraisals of "Outstanding" and “Exceptional” within the first two years of joining
•	Delivered end-to-end analysis and communications to generate over a million dollars’ worth of secured contract revenue, including the renewal of two of our key accounts
•	Spearheaded the global portfolio valuations of two of the largest family businesses in the Middle East, including constructing income and market approach models, analyzing and visualizing market and industry data, and managing written communications and in-person presentations with clients
•	Mobilized and counseled my junior team to consign various data-driven deliverables and written reports to various international clients in the artificial intelligence, heavy machinery distribution, cybersecurity, hygiene, paper printing, and poultry sectors

•	Winner of two Shukran Star awards within six months of joining
•	Conducted various market approach valuations of major players in the MENA event management, healthcare, oil drilling, automotive e-auction, and food delivery aggregator sector, resulting in multi-million dollar M&A transactions
•	Conducted an extensive feasibility study and strategic roadmap for the establishment of a MENA-specific video-on-demand platform
•	Participated as a keynote presenter to young Saudi entrepreneurs as part of Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Communications and Information’s Ebtaker program

I received a 4.85 rating out of 5 in EY Feedback Reports after performing varied discounted cash flow and market approach valuation models for poultry, smart grid, and submarine cable companies. My team's substantial market feasibility research and competitor analyses spearheaded the entry of three firms into the MENA region and resulted in an 80% client acquisition rate for EY. I also regularly mediated client expectations with our team's valuation based on projected income streams.

TrashTalk is a student-led social initiative targeting the littering epidemic in the MENA region, namely Jordan and the UAE. It consists of a multimedia social commentary conveyed to the Arab youth via smart bin installations, the sale of merchandise, and a social media movement. The aim is to reprogram the youth's cultural mentality and introspective outlook towards their role in society. We are currently seeking approval to manufacture and install our smartbin mockups on Amman's streets.

I worked on-site with a client and an EY team in verifying and updating financial statements for two major F&B sister companies in the Gulf under critical deadlines. Besides translating international purchase orders, I established a digital archive for our client as an alternative to its paper-based culture which is still in use today.

about:
Living in Paris, France since August 2023 and Milan, Italy from April 2024, I deepened my expertise in marketing and strategy through the HEC Paris and SDA Bocconi MBA programs.

In the summer of 2024, I completed the French Way of the Camino de Santiago, walking 779 kilometers over 35 days through Northern Spain — an experience that reaffirmed my commitment to refining my resilience, self-awareness, and adaptability.

In February 2025, I joined Strategy& (PwC’s strategy consulting practice) in Tokyo, where I continue to broaden my horizons by helping organizations transform and grow in a rapidly evolving global landscape.

With 10 years of international experience — including three years of childhood and five years in key professional roles across Los Angeles, Kansas City, and Chicago — I remain passionate about corporate strategy and innovation as a strategy consultant, and about bridging the healthcare realm as a registered pharmacist, to create meaningful impact across industries and society as a whole.

In this role, I had the opportunity to work on some high-impact projects such as:

publications.title: A Preliminary Study of the Effects of Racialization and Humanness on the Verbal Abuse of Female-Gendered Robots
publications.publishedAt: Companion of the 2018 ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction · Mar 1, 2018
publications.description: Recent research has indicated that people engage, and unabashedly so, in the verbal abuse of female-gendered robots. To understand whether this also cuts across racial lines, and furthermore, whether it differs from objectifying treatment of actual people, we conducted a preliminary mixed-methods investigation of online commentary on videos of three such robots -- Bina48, Nadine, and YangYang -- contrasted with commentary on videos of three women with similar identity cues. Analysis of the frequency and nature of abusive commentary suggests that: (1) the verbal abuse of the Bina48 and YangYang (two robots racialized as Black and Asian respectively) is laced with both subtle and overt racism; (2) people more readily engage in the verbal abuse of humanlike robots (versus other people). Not only do these findings reflect a concerning phenomenon, but consideration is also warranted as to whether people’s engagement in abusive interactions with humanlike robots could impact their subsequent interactions with other people.
